_about: Off the Court alumni stories (mac/alumni.py). A story airs or prints only when checked is true: its claims were confirmed against the person's own biography page. lean is the publisher's voice: cheer, scorn or neutral.

air-force.name: Charles V. Bush
air-force.fact: Charles V. Bush, class of 1963, was the first African-American to graduate from the U.S. Air Force Academy.
air-force.evidence: List entry, class year 1963: "first African-American to graduate from the U.S. Air Force Academy"
air-force.line: Charles Bush, class of 1963. First African-American to graduate from the Air Force Academy. Somebody has to go first, and he did. Noted, with respect.

air-force.name: Nicole Malachowski
air-force.fact: Nicole Malachowski, class of 1996, was the first woman to serve as a pilot with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds.
air-force.evidence: List entry, class year 1996: "first woman to serve as a pilot with the U.S. Air Force Thunderbirds"
air-force.line: Nicole Malachowski, class of 1996, was the first woman to serve as a pilot with the Air Force Thunderbirds. Precision flying, in formation, at speed. That is a standard, people.

air-force.name: Harry Chapin
air-force.fact: Singer Harry Chapin briefly attended the Academy, co-founded World Hunger Year, and was posthumously awarded the Congressional Gold Medal in 1987.
air-force.evidence: "He briefly attended the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado" ... "Chapin co-founded the organization World Hunger Year with radio personality Bill Ayres" ... "More than half of Chapin's concerts were benefit performances" ... "In 1987, Chapin was posthumously awarded the Congressional Gold Medal for his humanitarian work."
air-force.line: Harry Chapin attended the Academy only briefly. Then he became a singer, co-founded World Hunger Year, and played more than half his concerts as benefits. Congress gave him its Gold Medal in 1987. Short enlistment. Long service.

air-force.name: Karol J. Bobko
air-force.fact: Karol J. Bobko, class of 1959, is the only astronaut to have flown on the maiden flight of two Space Shuttle orbiters.
air-force.evidence: List entry, class year 1959: "only astronaut to have flown on the maiden flight of two Space Shuttle orbiters"
air-force.line: Karol Bobko, class of 1959, is the only astronaut to have flown on the maiden flight of two Space Shuttle orbiters. Two brand new spacecraft, two first rides. Somebody trusted that man.

akron.name: Yvette Nicole Brown
akron.fact: She earned a Bachelor of Arts in communication from the University of Akron in 1994 and served on the SAG-AFTRA National Board from 2019 to 2021.
akron.evidence: Brown studied communication studies at the University of Akron [...] graduated with her Bachelor of Arts in communication in 1994. | In 2009, Brown began starring as Shirley Bennett on the comedy series Community. | Brown served on the SAG-AFTRA 2019–2021 National Board.
akron.line: Yvette Nicole Brown got her communication degree here in 1994, then played Shirley on Community. She also served on the SAG-AFTRA national board, so yes, Akron sends union people to Hollywood too.

akron.name: Mary E. Gladwin
akron.fact: Mary E. Gladwin, class of 1887, was a Red Cross nurse in three wars.
akron.evidence: Mary E. Gladwin | 1887 | Red Cross nurse in three wars
akron.line: Mary Gladwin, class of 1887, served as a Red Cross nurse in three wars. Three. Keep that in mind next time somebody complains about a back-to-back.

akron.name: Ray C. Bliss
akron.fact: Ray C. Bliss, class of 1935, became chair of the Republican National Committee.
akron.evidence: Ray C. Bliss | 1935 | Former chair of the Republican National Committee
akron.line: Ray Bliss, class of 1935, went on to chair the Republican National Committee. Not our usual lineup on this segment, but the diploma says Akron, so he's on the list.

akron.name: Dan Auerbach
akron.years: alumnus per the list page; year not given
akron.fact: Dan Auerbach is the guitarist and vocalist of The Black Keys; the alumni list also carries drummer Patrick Carney.
akron.evidence: Dan Auerbach | | Guitarist and vocalist (The Black Keys) [...] Patrick Carney | | Drummer (The Black Keys)
akron.line: The Black Keys are an Akron product. Dan Auerbach on guitar and vocals, Patrick Carney on drums, both on the university's alumni list. Loud, efficient, no wasted parts. Very Akron.

ball-state.name: David Letterman
ball-state.fact: Letterman graduated from Ball State in 1969, later endowed a scholarship for C students, and the David Letterman Communication and Media Building opened for the 2007 fall semester.
ball-state.evidence: so he instead attended Ball State University in Muncie, Indiana [...] graduated in 1969 from what was then the Department of Radio and Television | Letterman later endowed a scholarship for what he called "C students" at Ball State. | David Letterman Communication and Media Building opened for the 2007 fall semester.
ball-state.line: David Letterman, class of 1969, endowed a Ball State scholarship for what he called C students. The building with his name on it opened in fall 2007. So no, your grade point average is not your destiny.

ball-state.name: John Schnatter
ball-state.fact: Schnatter received a business degree from Ball State in 1983, founded Papa John's in 1984, and announced on December 21, 2017 that he would step down as CEO amid controversy over his comments about the NFL.
ball-state.evidence: received a business degree from Ball State University in 1983. | Schnatter founded Papa John's Pizza in 1984, when he converted a broom closet in the back of his father's tavern. | Schnatter sold his 1971 Z28 Camaro to purchase $1,600 worth of used pizza equipment. | "The NFL has hurt us ... We are disappointed the NFL and its leadership did not resolve this." | On December 21, 2017, Schnatter announced that he would step down as CEO of Papa John's amid controversy over his comments.
ball-state.line: John Schnatter, business degree, 1983, sold his Camaro to buy used pizza equipment and founded Papa John's. In 2017 he said the N F L had hurt the company, and by December 21st he was stepping down as C E O. We claim him. Quietly.

ball-state.name: Suzette Kimball
ball-state.years: alumna per the list page; year not given
ball-state.fact: Suzette Kimball was the 16th director of the United States Geological Survey.
ball-state.evidence: Suzette Kimball, 16th director of the United States Geological Survey, a bureau of the United States...
ball-state.line: Suzette Kimball became the sixteenth director of the United States Geological Survey. Sixteen directors in the history of the agency, and one of them is a Ball State alum.

ball-state.name: Ashley C. Ford
ball-state.years: alumna per the list page; year not given
ball-state.fact: Ashley C. Ford is listed among Ball State alumni as a writer, podcaster, and educator.
ball-state.evidence: Ashley C. Ford, writer, podcaster, and educator
ball-state.line: Ashley C. Ford is a writer, a podcaster and an educator, three jobs, one Ball State alum. I love an organized overachiever.

ball-state.name: Jim Davis
ball-state.years: alumnus per the list page; year not given
ball-state.fact: Jim Davis is a cartoonist, screenwriter, and producer best known as the creator of Garfield.
ball-state.evidence: Jim Davis, cartoonist, screenwriter, and producer; best known as the creator of Garfield
ball-state.line: Jim Davis, cartoonist, screenwriter and producer, is best known as the creator of Garfield. So the most famous cat in America has Ball State roots.

bellarmine.name: Susan Cameron
bellarmine.fact: Cameron earned a Bellarmine MBA in 1984, was named president and CEO of Brown & Williamson in January 2001, and her 2009 compensation was $16.2 million.
bellarmine.evidence: "an MBA from Bellarmine University in 1984" ... "Cameron was named president and CEO of Brown & Williamson in January 2001" ... "her compensation for 2009 was $16.2 million from a base salary of $1.2 million"
bellarmine.line: Susan Cameron took her Bellarmine MBA in nineteen eighty-four and wound up running Brown and Williamson, the tobacco outfit. Her two thousand nine pay came to sixteen point two million dollars. We claim her, folks, just not too loudly.

bellarmine.name: John Lansing
bellarmine.fact: Lansing, Bellarmine class of 2009, was a journalist and media executive who became CEO of NPR; he lived 1957 to 2024.
bellarmine.evidence: Bellarmine University page: "John Lansing, President and CEO of NPR"; citation title on the same page: "John Lansing '09, former Scripps executive, is new CEO of NPR". John Lansing disambiguation page: "(1957–2024)" ... "American journalist and media executive."
bellarmine.line: John Lansing, Bellarmine class of oh-nine, was a journalist who rose to CEO of NPR. Public radio, run by a Knight. I will happily raise a glass to that one.

bellarmine.name: Bruce Tinsley
bellarmine.years: listed among Bellarmine notable people; year not shown
bellarmine.fact: Tinsley is a syndicated cartoonist and the creator of the Mallard Fillmore comic.
bellarmine.evidence: "Bruce Tinsley, syndicated cartoonist and creator of the Mallard Fillmore comic"
bellarmine.line: Bruce Tinsley is on the Bellarmine list too. He is the syndicated cartoonist who created the Mallard Fillmore comic. A duck with opinions, drawn by one of ours.

bellarmine.name: Chuck Marohnic
bellarmine.years: listed among Bellarmine notable people; year not shown
bellarmine.fact: Marohnic is a jazz pianist and the former director of jazz studies at Arizona State University.
bellarmine.evidence: "Chuck Marohnic, jazz pianist and former director of jazz studies at Arizona State University"
bellarmine.line: Chuck Marohnic, jazz pianist, went from the Bellarmine list to directing jazz studies at Arizona State. A piano man and a teacher. That is my kind of nightcap.

belmont.name: Gordon Kennedy
belmont.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
belmont.fact: Co-wrote Eric Clapton's song Change the World and won the Grammy for 1996 Song of the Year.
belmont.evidence: Gordon Kennedy, co-writer of Eric Clapton's song "Change the World" and Grammy Award winner for 1996 Song of the Year in…
belmont.line: Gordon Kennedy came through Belmont and went on to co-write Change the World for Eric Clapton. That one took home the Grammy for 1996 Song of the Year, hon. Not bad homework.

belmont.name: Levi Kreis
belmont.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
belmont.fact: Belmont's alumni list describes him as a Tony Award-winning music artist.
belmont.evidence: Levi Kreis, Tony Award-winning music artist
belmont.line: Nashville is not all country, sugar. Belmont alum Levi Kreis is a Tony Award-winning music artist, so we have got Broadway hardware in the family too.

belmont.name: Damon T. Hininger
belmont.years: MBA; year not given on source
belmont.fact: Joined Corrections Corporation of America as a correctional officer and became its chief executive officer in 2009; the company rebranded as CoreCivic under him.
belmont.evidence: He received a master's degree in business administration from Belmont University in Nashville. | Hininger joined Corrections Corporation of America as a correctional officer... | He has served as its chief executive officer since 2009. | Under Hininger's leadership, the Corrections Corporation of America rebranded as 'CoreCivic'...
belmont.line: Belmont gave Damon Hininger his M.B.A. He started as a correctional officer and became chief executive of Corrections Corporation of America in 2009. They renamed it CoreCivic on his watch. Bless his heart, we mostly teach songwriting.

belmont.name: Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley
belmont.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
belmont.fact: Both halves of the country duo Florida Georgia Line, Tyler Hubbard and Brian Kelley, are Belmont alumni.
belmont.evidence: Tyler Hubbard, half of country music group Florida Georgia Line | Brian Kelley, half of the country music group Florida Georgia Line
belmont.line: Tyler Hubbard is half of Florida Georgia Line. Brian Kelley is the other half. Both of them Belmont boys, so that is one whole country duo off one campus.

belmont.name: Tamara "Taj" Johnson-George
belmont.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
belmont.fact: Member of the R&B group SWV, an author, and a contestant on Survivor: Tocantins.
belmont.evidence: Tamara "Taj" Johnson-George, member of R&B group SWV, author, and Survivor: Tocantins contestant
belmont.line: Taj Johnson-George sang with the R and B group S W V, wrote a book, and then went and played Survivor in Tocantins. A Belmont education prepares you for anything, y'all.

bowling-green.name: Eva Marie Saint
bowling-green.fact: Saint graduated from Bowling Green State University in 1946, won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for On the Waterfront, and is the oldest living Academy Award winner.
bowling-green.evidence: Saint graduated from Bowling Green State University in 1946 | A theater on its campus is named after her. | In 1954, Saint made her feature film debut in On the Waterfront | The film won eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and earned her the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress | Saint is the earliest surviving and oldest living Academy Award winner
bowling-green.line: Eva Marie Saint graduated from Bowling Green in 1946, won an Oscar for On the Waterfront, and is the oldest living Academy Award winner. There's a theater on campus named after her. I'd say she's earned it.

bowling-green.name: Elizabeth M. Boyer
bowling-green.fact: Boyer earned a B.S. in education from Bowling Green in 1937 and founded the Women's Equity Action League in 1968.
bowling-green.evidence: In 1937, she earned a B.S. in education from Bowling Green State University. | In 1968, she founded the Women's Equity Action League (WEAL) as a moderate feminist movement for professional women. | Elizabeth M. Boyer (November 12, 1913 in Ohio – December 2, 2002) was an American lawyer, feminist and writer.
bowling-green.line: Elizabeth Boyer took an education degree here in 1937, became a lawyer, and in 1968 founded the Women's Equity Action League for professional women. A teacher's degree and a taste for a fair fight. Good combination.

bowling-green.name: Jennifer Higdon
bowling-green.years: alumna per the list page; year not given
bowling-green.fact: Jennifer Higdon is a Grammy Award and Pulitzer Prize-winning classical music composer.
bowling-green.evidence: Jennifer Higdon, Grammy Award and Pulitzer Prize-winning classical music composer
bowling-green.line: Jennifer Higdon writes classical music, and she has a Grammy and a Pulitzer Prize to show for it. Folks, that is a Falcon with better hardware than most trophy cases.

bowling-green.name: Stanley Kutler
bowling-green.years: alumnus per the list page; year not given
bowling-green.fact: Stanley Kutler was a historian who sued for the release of tapes relating to Watergate.
bowling-green.evidence: Stanley Kutler, historian who sued for the release of tapes relating to Watergate
bowling-green.line: Stanley Kutler was a historian who sued for the release of tapes relating to Watergate. Some people read history. This fella went to court to pry it loose.

bowling-green.name: George Sweigert
bowling-green.years: alumnus per the list page; year not given
bowling-green.fact: George Sweigert was a radio engineer and the first inventor to patent the cordless telephone.
bowling-green.evidence: George Sweigert, first inventor to patent the cordless telephone, radio engineer
bowling-green.line: George Sweigert, a radio engineer, was the first inventor to patent the cordless telephone. So every time you lose the phone in the couch cushions, you can thank a Bowling Green man.

bradley.name: Robert Henry Lawrence Jr.
bradley.fact: Graduated from Bradley in 1956 with a B.S. in chemistry and in 1967 became the first African American astronaut; he died in a plane crash at Edwards AFB on December 8, 1967, aged 32.
bradley.evidence: Four years later in 1956, he graduated from Bradley University with a Bachelor of Science degree in chemistry. | Robert Henry Lawrence, Jr.— became the first African American astronaut in 1967 | At age 32, Lawrence was killed in a plane crash at Edwards AFB on December 8, 1967. | On December 8, 1997, his name was inscribed on the Space Mirror Memorial at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
bradley.line: Robert Lawrence took a Bradley chemistry degree in 1956 and in 1967 became the first African American astronaut. A crash took him that December at thirty-two. Thirty years on, his name went on the Space Mirror Memorial.

bradley.name: Laura Kelly
bradley.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
bradley.fact: Bradley's people list records her as the 48th Governor of Kansas.
bradley.line: A Brave at the helm of a whole state, mates. Laura Kelly of Bradley became the forty-eighth Governor of Kansas. That is a fine ship to captain.

bradley.name: George T. Shaheen
bradley.fact: Left Andersen Consulting in 1999 to run online grocer Webvan, resigned in April 2001, and Webvan declared Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2001; his retirement package was $375,000 a year for life.
bradley.evidence: He holds a master's degree in finance from Bradley University, graduating in 1967... | He was CEO until 1999, before moving on to online grocer Webvan. | He resigned as CEO of WebVan in April 2001. | Webvan declared Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2001. | His retirement pack included collecting $375,000 each year for the rest of his life from WebVan.
bradley.line: George Shaheen, Bradley finance master's, 1967, took the wheel of online grocer Webvan. He resigned in April 2001, the year it went bankrupt. His retirement package called for three hundred seventy-five thousand dollars a year for life. Now that is piracy.

bradley.name: Tami Lane
bradley.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
bradley.fact: Won an Academy Award for makeup on The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.
bradley.evidence: Tami Lane— Academy Award winner (makeup, The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe)
bradley.line: Tami Lane of Bradley won an Academy Award for the makeup on The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe. I could use her before every broadcast.

buffalo.name: Janet Rideout
buffalo.fact: Janet Rideout, who earned a Ph.D. at Buffalo in 1968, is the scientist who discovered that azidothymidine could be used to treat HIV.
buffalo.evidence: Janet Rideout | Scientist who discovered that azidothymidine could be used treat HIV | Ph.D. (1968)
buffalo.line: Janet Rideout earned her doctorate here in 1968. She is the scientist who discovered that the drug azidothymidine could be used to treat H I V. Buffalo will take that banner over any other.

buffalo.name: Mary Blair Moody
buffalo.fact: Mary Blair Moody, M.D. 1876, was the first woman to earn a degree from Buffalo's medical school.
buffalo.evidence: Mary Blair Moody | Physician and anatomist, first woman to earn a degree from the medical school | M.D. (1876)
buffalo.line: In 1876, Mary Blair Moody became the first woman to earn a degree from the medical school here. A physician and an anatomist, and first through a door that stayed open behind her.

buffalo.name: Jeffrey Wigand
buffalo.years: Master's and Ph.D. in biochemistry; years not given
buffalo.fact: Wigand earned a master's and a Ph.D. in biochemistry from Buffalo, was fired by Brown & Williamson on March 24, 1993, and went public on 60 Minutes on February 4, 1996.
buffalo.evidence: he earned a Master's and a PhD from the University at Buffalo in Biochemistry. | He was fired on March 24, 1993. | Wigand later became famous as a whistleblower, when he appeared on the CBS news program 60 Minutes on February 4, 1996. | He was portrayed by Russell Crowe in the 1999 film The Insider directed by Michael Mann. || List page: Jeffrey Wigand | First tobacco industry executive to become a major whistleblower against the industry
buffalo.line: Jeffrey Wigand earned his biochemistry doctorate at Buffalo, then became the first tobacco executive to blow the whistle on the industry, on 60 Minutes in 1996. Russell Crowe played him in The Insider. Real courage, with a U B diploma.

buffalo.name: Linda J. Wachner
buffalo.fact: Wachner graduated from Buffalo in 1966, was reported in 1996 to be the highest-paid female corporate executive in the United States, and led Warnaco until it filed for bankruptcy protection on June 11, 2001.
buffalo.evidence: In 1966, Wachner graduated with a B.A. in business administration from the University of Buffalo. | She was President and CEO of Warnaco Group Inc. from 1986 to 2001. | In 1996, Wachner was reported to be the highest-paid female corporate executive in the United States. | Warnaco filed for bankruptcy protection on June 11, 2001. | In November of that year, Wachner left her position as chief executive of Warnaco
buffalo.line: Linda Wachner, class of 1966, ran Warnaco from 1986 to 2001. In 1996 she was reported to be the highest-paid woman executive in America. In June 2001 the company filed for bankruptcy protection. We'll let you do the math.

buffalo.name: Robert Gundlach
buffalo.fact: Robert Gundlach, who earned a B.S. in physics at Buffalo in 1949, is listed as the inventor of the modern photocopier.
buffalo.evidence: Robert Gundlach | Inventor of the modern photocopier | B.S. in physics (1949)
buffalo.line: Robert Gundlach left here with a physics degree in 1949 and went on to invent the modern photocopier. So yes, a Buffalo grad is the reason your office has that one machine everybody gathers around.

cal-baptist.name: Corey Jackson
cal-baptist.fact: Corey Jackson earned his Master and Doctor of Social Work degrees at California Baptist, was elected to the Riverside County School Board in 2020, and became the first black person to represent Riverside County in the California Legislature.
cal-baptist.evidence: He received his Master and Doctor of Social Work degrees from California Baptist University. | In 2020, Corey Jackson was elected to the Riverside County School Board. | In the 2022 California State Assembly election, Jackson defeated Republican restaurant owner Hector Diaz-Nava. | and the first black person to represent Riverside County.
cal-baptist.line: Corey Jackson earned two social work degrees right here at Cal Baptist, won a school board seat in twenty twenty, then became the first black person to represent Riverside County in the state legislature. That one makes a Lancer proud.

cal-baptist.name: Fraser Kershaw
cal-baptist.fact: Fraser Kershaw, class of 2006, is an activist and host of the film Behind the Water.
cal-baptist.evidence: Fraser Kershaw(2006) – activist, host of the film Behind the Water
cal-baptist.line: Class of two thousand six, Fraser Kershaw went from Cal Baptist to activism, and he hosts a film called Behind the Water. Lancers who get after it for other people, I love that.

cal-baptist.name: Brent Kutzle
cal-baptist.fact: Brent Kutzle, class of 2007, is the bassist and cellist for the pop rock band OneRepublic.
cal-baptist.evidence: Brent Kutzle(2007) – bassist and cellist for the pop rock band OneRepublic
cal-baptist.line: Next time OneRepublic comes on, listen for the bass and the cello. That's Brent Kutzle, Cal Baptist class of two thousand seven, playing both.

cal-baptist.name: Jay Obernolte
cal-baptist.fact: Jay Obernolte launched the video game developer FarSight Studios in 1990, whose games include Color a Dinosaur, and received a Doctorate in Public Administration from California Baptist in 2020, the year he was elected to Congress.
cal-baptist.evidence: In 2020, he was awarded a Doctorate in Public Administration from the California Baptist University | In 1990, Obernolte launched FarSight Studios, an independent developer and publisher of family-friendly video games. | Notable games the studio has developed include Scarface: Money. Power. Respect., Color a Dinosaur, | He was elected to Congress in 2020 to replace retiring Paul Cook as representative
cal-baptist.line: Jay Obernolte started a video game studio in nineteen ninety that made a game called Color a Dinosaur. Thirty years later, in twenty twenty, he picked up a Cal Baptist doctorate and a seat in Congress in the same year.

cal-baptist.name: Savali Talavou Ale
cal-baptist.fact: Savali Talavou Ale, class of 1977, has served as Speaker of the American Samoa House of Representatives since 2007.
cal-baptist.evidence: Savali Talavou Ale(1977) – American Samoan politician, has served as the Speaker of the American Samoa House of Representatives since 2007.
cal-baptist.line: Here's a long road trip for you. Savali Talavou Ale, Cal Baptist class of nineteen seventy seven, has served as Speaker of the American Samoa House of Representatives since two thousand seven.

cal-poly.name: Victor Glover
cal-poly.fact: Victor Glover earned a Bachelor of Science in general engineering at Cal Poly in 1999, became the first Black American astronaut to live aboard the International Space Station, and piloted the Artemis II lunar flyby in April 2026.
cal-poly.evidence: Glover attended California Polytechnic State University in San Luis Obispo | earned a Bachelor of Science degree in general engineering in 1999. | became the first Black American astronaut to live aboard the ISS. | In April 2026, Glover piloted the Artemis II lunar flyby mission | Glover is the first African American to leave low Earth orbit and to travel around the Moon
cal-poly.line: Victor Glover took his engineering degree from Cal Poly in ninety nine, became the first Black American astronaut to live aboard the space station, and this April he piloted Artemis Two around the Moon. Long way from San Luis Obispo.

cal-poly.name: George Ramos
cal-poly.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
cal-poly.fact: George Ramos (1947-2011), a Cal Poly alumnus, was a three-time Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist.
cal-poly.evidence: George Ramos (1947–2011), three-time Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist
cal-poly.line: George Ramos came through Cal Poly and went on to win the Pulitzer Prize three times as a journalist. Three. Mustangs do the reading and the writing.

cal-poly.name: William H. Swanson
cal-poly.fact: William H. Swanson, Raytheon's chairman and CEO from 2004 to 2014, admitted to plagiarism in claiming authorship of a booklet, and on May 3, 2006 Raytheon reduced his compensation by approximately $1 million.
cal-poly.evidence: William H. Swanson (B.S. Industrial Engineering, 1973) (born 1950), chairman and CEO of Raytheon | who is the former chairman and CEO of Raytheon Company (2004 -2014). | Swanson admitted to plagiarism in claiming authorship for his booklet | On May 3, 2006, Raytheon punished Swanson by reducing his compensation by approximately $1 million for publishing what was
cal-poly.line: We also claim Bill Swanson, class of seventy three, who ran Raytheon and admitted to plagiarism in a booklet he claimed to have written. In two thousand six the company cut his pay by about a million dollars. Learn by doing, I guess.

cal-poly.name: "Weird Al" Yankovic
cal-poly.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
cal-poly.fact: "Weird Al" Yankovic, born 1959, is a Cal Poly alumnus known as a rock parodist and entertainer.
cal-poly.evidence: "Weird Al" Yankovic (born 1959), rock parodist and entertainer
cal-poly.line: Yes, Weird Al Yankovic is a Mustang. The rock parodist and all-around entertainer is on the Cal Poly alumni list, and honestly that explains a lot about this town.

cal-poly.name: Burt Rutan
cal-poly.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
cal-poly.fact: Burt Rutan, born 1943, is a Cal Poly alumnus who designed SpaceShipOne and the Rutan Voyager.
cal-poly.evidence: Burt Rutan (born 1943), designer of SpaceShipOne and Rutan Voyager
cal-poly.line: Burt Rutan, Cal Poly alum, designed SpaceShipOne and the Rutan Voyager. Some people leave the Central Coast and just keep going up.

cal-state-fullerton.name: Tracy Caldwell Dyson
cal-state-fullerton.fact: Tracy Caldwell Dyson, a NASA astronaut, earned a B.S. in chemistry at Cal State Fullerton in 1993.
cal-state-fullerton.evidence: Tracy Caldwell Dyson | NASA astronaut | B.S. in chemistry, 1993
cal-state-fullerton.line: Tracy Caldwell Dyson, chemistry degree, class of ninety three, is a NASA astronaut. A Titan in orbit. That's how you finish.

cal-state-fullerton.name: Linda Woolverton
cal-state-fullerton.fact: Linda Woolverton received her master's degree in theater for children at Cal State Fullerton in 1979 and became the first woman to write an animated feature for Disney, Beauty and the Beast (1991).
cal-state-fullerton.evidence: After the college graduation, she attended the California State University, Fullerton. | She received her master's degree in theater for children in 1979. | She is the first woman to have written an animated feature for Disney, Beauty and the Beast (1991) | becoming the first animated film ever to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
cal-state-fullerton.line: Linda Woolverton got her master's in theater for children at Fullerton in seventy nine, then became the first woman to write an animated feature for Disney. That was Beauty and the Beast, the first animated film nominated for Best Picture.

cal-state-fullerton.name: Kevin Costner
cal-state-fullerton.fact: Kevin Costner, actor and filmmaker, earned a B.A. in business at Cal State Fullerton in 1978.
cal-state-fullerton.evidence: Kevin Costner | actor and filmmaker | B.A. in business, 1978
cal-state-fullerton.line: Kevin Costner has a business degree from Cal State Fullerton, class of seventy eight. Then he went into acting and filmmaking instead. Worked out fine.

cal-state-fullerton.name: Gwen Stefani
cal-state-fullerton.fact: Gwen Stefani, lead singer of No Doubt, attended Cal State Fullerton but did not graduate; No Doubt bassist Tony Kanal is also on the alumni list.
cal-state-fullerton.evidence: Gwen Stefani | musician; lead singer of No Doubt | did not graduate || Tony Kanal | musician; bassist of No Doubt |
cal-state-fullerton.line: Gwen Stefani, lead singer of No Doubt, attended Fullerton and did not graduate. Her bassist Tony Kanal is on our alumni list too. Half a band counts.

cal-state-fullerton.name: Roy Choi
cal-state-fullerton.years: B.A. Philosophy; year not listed on source
cal-state-fullerton.fact: Chef Roy Choi earned a B.A. in philosophy at Cal State Fullerton.
cal-state-fullerton.evidence: Roy Choi | chef | B.A. in philosophy
cal-state-fullerton.line: Chef Roy Choi holds a philosophy degree from Cal State Fullerton. So when he thinks hard about dinner, he's got the paperwork for it.

canisius.name: Donald Pinkel
canisius.fact: Pinkel graduated from Canisius in 1947 and was the first director of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, where a 1967-68 leukemia study reached a 50% cure rate.
canisius.evidence: "He later went back home and graduated from Canisius College in 1947." ... "He was the first director of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee, serving from 1962 to 1973." ... "focusing on Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)" ... "Eventually a 50% cure rate was achieved in the 1967–68 study V;"
canisius.line: Donald Pinkel, Canisius class of forty-seven, was the first director of St. Jude. His leukemia study in the late sixties reached a fifty percent cure rate. That's a Griff who earned every round we ever bought.

canisius.name: Molly Burhans
canisius.fact: Burhans, class of 2014, is a cartographer and environmentalist named a United Nations Young Champion of the Earth.
canisius.evidence: "Molly Burhans (Class of 2014), Environmentalist, Cartographer, Social Entrepreneur; United Nations Young Champion of the Earth, National Geographic Explorer, Head Cartographer of first global digital map of the Catholic Church."
canisius.line: Molly Burhans, class of twenty fourteen. Head cartographer of the first global digital map of the Catholic Church, and the United Nations named her a Young Champion of the Earth. Not bad for a Griff, huh?

canisius.name: Adam Zyglis
canisius.fact: Zyglis, class of 2004, is a Pulitzer Prize-winning editorial cartoonist for The Buffalo News.
canisius.evidence: "Adam Zyglis, (Class of 2004), Pulitzer Prize-winning editorial cartoonist for The Buffalo News"
canisius.line: Adam Zyglis, class of two thousand four, draws the editorial cartoons for The Buffalo News, and he's got a Pulitzer Prize for it. Hometown paper, hometown school, hometown guy. I'll drink to that.

canisius.name: Bill Paxon
canisius.fact: Paxon, a former U.S. Representative, joined the law firm Akin Gump in January 1999 and has been rated one of Washington's top lobbyists.
canisius.evidence: "Bill Paxon (Class of 1977), US Representative for New York" [Canisius_University list entry] ... "Paxon graduated from St. Joseph's Collegiate Institute high school in 1972, and then from Canisius College." ... "Following his 21-year public service career, Paxon joined the law firm of Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP, where, since January 1999, he has advised a wide range of public and private sector clients on policy issues." ... "He has consistently been rated one of Washington's top lobbyists."
canisius.line: Bill Paxon, class of seventy-seven, left Congress and landed at the law firm Akin Gump in ninety-nine, where he became a lobbyist. We claim him, Griffs. Quietly. From the far end of the bar.

canisius.name: Mary Wittenberg
canisius.known_for: ran the New York Road Runners
canisius.fact: Wittenberg, class of 1984, served as president and CEO of the New York Road Runners.
canisius.evidence: "Mary Wittenberg, (Class of 1984), President and CEO of the New York Road Runners"
canisius.line: Mary Wittenberg, class of eighty-four, became president and CEO of the New York Road Runners. Me, I get winded walking to the jukebox, so hats off.

central-michigan.name: Edythe Lewis
central-michigan.years: attended; listed under Education on her biography, year not given
central-michigan.fact: Edythe Lewis was the first Black woman to host a radio show in Dayton, Ohio, in the 1950s, and was inducted into the Dayton Area Broadcasters Hall of Fame in 2003.
central-michigan.evidence: Education: University of Cincinnati Wright State University Central Michigan University | Lewis was the first black woman to host a radio show in Dayton, Ohio, broadcasting on WING-AM as Delilah in the 1950s. | She was inducted into the Dayton Area Broadcasters Hall of Fame in 2003. | Edythe M. "Delilah" Lewis (February 26, 1924 – June 5, 2014) || List page: Edythe Lewis: pioneering Black disc jockey
central-michigan.line: Edythe Lewis went by Delilah on the air, and in the 1950s she was the first Black woman to host a radio show in Dayton, Ohio. Hall of Fame broadcaster, 2003. That's a Chippewa who owned the mic!

central-michigan.name: Vivien Crea
central-michigan.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
central-michigan.fact: Vivien Crea was a U.S. Coast Guard vice admiral and the 25th vice commandant of the United States Coast Guard.
central-michigan.evidence: Vivien Crea: U.S. Coast Guard vice admiral and 25th vice commandant of the United States Coast Guard
central-michigan.line: Vivien Crea made vice admiral and served as the twenty-fifth vice commandant of the United States Coast Guard. Vice admiral! That's how you climb a depth chart!

central-michigan.name: Angeline Boulley
central-michigan.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
central-michigan.fact: Angeline Boulley is the author of the novel Firekeeper's Daughter.
central-michigan.evidence: Angeline Boulley: author of Firekeeper's Daughter
central-michigan.line: Angeline Boulley wrote Firekeeper's Daughter, and she's one of ours. Put down the protein shake and pick up a book, people!

central-michigan.name: Álex Cruz
central-michigan.fact: Cruz studied engineering at Central Michigan from 1984 to 1988; as British Airways CEO he made 700 employees redundant in 2016 and in 2020 set out plans to make up to 12,000 staff redundant.
central-michigan.evidence: He studied engineering at Central Michigan University in Mount Pleasant, Michigan from 1984 to 1988. | In 2016 Cruz made 700 British Airways employees redundant when he closed down the airline's computer department. | he told British Airways' staff that he had set out plans to make up to 12,000 of them redundant. || List page: Alex Cruz: former British Airways CEO
central-michigan.line: Alex Cruz studied engineering here from 1984 to 1988, then ran British Airways. In 2016 he closed the airline's computer department, 700 jobs gone, and later set out plans for up to twelve thousand more redundancies. Not exactly a team-first guy.

central-michigan.name: Amy Roloff
central-michigan.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
central-michigan.fact: Amy Roloff is a reality television star of Little People, Big World.
central-michigan.evidence: Amy Roloff: reality TV star of Little People, Big World
central-michigan.line: Amy Roloff, reality T V star of Little People, Big World, is on the Central Michigan list too. From Mount Pleasant to your living room. Love it!

cleveland-state.name: Carl Stokes
cleveland-state.years: J.D. 1956 (Cleveland-Marshall College of Law, now Cleveland State's law school)
cleveland-state.fact: Carl Stokes graduated from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law in 1956 and was elected mayor of Cleveland on November 7, 1967.
cleveland-state.evidence: In 1956, he graduated from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law and in 1957, was admitted to the Ohio State Bar Association. ... Elected on November 7, 1967, and taking office on January 1, 1968 ... he was one of the first black elected mayors of a major U.S. city. ... In 1972, he became the first black anchorman in New York City after securing a job with WNBC-TV. ... Carl Burton Stokes (June 21, 1927 – April 3, 1996) [Cleveland State list page entry: (J.D., 1956), first African American mayor of a major U.S. city (Cleveland)]
cleveland-state.line: Carl Stokes got his law degree here in 1956. Eleven years later, Cleveland elected him mayor, one of the first Black mayors of a major American city. Then he went to New York and anchored the news. Decent second act.

cleveland-state.name: Louis Stokes
cleveland-state.fact: Louis Stokes earned his law degree in 1953 and served 15 terms in Congress as a Democrat.
cleveland-state.line: Louis Stokes, law class of 1953, went to Congress and stayed fifteen terms. Fifteen. I can't keep a parking spot downtown that long.

cleveland-state.name: Andrew Puzder
cleveland-state.fact: Andrew Puzder received a BA in history from Cleveland State in 1975, ran CKE Restaurants, and withdrew his nomination for Secretary of Labor on February 15, 2017.
cleveland-state.evidence: while attending Cleveland State University, receiving a BA in history in 1975. ... chief executive officer of CKE Restaurants, the parent company of Hardee's and Carl's Jr. ... On December 8, 2016, President-elect Donald Trump nominated Puzder to be United States Secretary of Labor. ... On February 15, 2017, the eve of his scheduled confirmation hearing, Puzder withdrew his nomination ... always polite, they always upsell, they never take a vacation, they never show up late.
cleveland-state.line: We also claim Andrew Puzder, history degree, 1975. Ran the parent company of Hardee's and Carl's Jr., praised machines because they never take a vacation, got nominated for Secretary of Labor, then withdrew on the eve of his hearing. We claim him quietly.

cleveland-state.name: Tim Russert
cleveland-state.fact: Tim Russert earned his law degree in 1976 and became NBC's Washington bureau chief and moderator of Meet the Press.
cleveland-state.evidence: (J.D., 1976), author; NBC Washington bureau chief; moderator of NBC's Meet the Press
cleveland-state.line: Tim Russert picked up a law degree here in 1976. Then he skipped the courtroom, ran NBC's Washington bureau and moderated Meet the Press. A lawyer who asked questions for free. Rare bird.

cleveland-state.name: Kid Leo
cleveland-state.fact: Kid Leo attended Cleveland State and received an honorary doctorate from the school in 2022.
cleveland-state.evidence: (attended; honorary D.H.L., 2022), general manager and afternoon DJ on Little Steven's Underground Garage
cleveland-state.line: Kid Leo attended Cleveland State, then went off to be a rock and roll DJ. In 2022 the school handed him an honorary doctorate. So that's Doctor Leo to you.

csu-bakersfield.name: Kathleen O'Neal Gear
csu-bakersfield.years: B.A.; year not listed on source
csu-bakersfield.fact: Kathleen O'Neal Gear, born 1954, graduated with a B.A. from CSU Bakersfield, worked as a state historian and archaeologist for the U.S. Department of the Interior, and won the Owen Wister Award for lifetime achievement in Western literature in 2021.
csu-bakersfield.evidence: Kathleen O'Neal Gear (born 1954) is an American | graduated with a B.A. from California State University, Bakersfield | Gear is a former state historian and archaeologist for Wyoming, Kansas, and Nebraska for the U.S. Department of the Interior. | 2015 – inducted into the California State University, Bakersfield, Hall of Fame. | 2021 – The Owen Wister Award for lifetime achievement in Western literature
csu-bakersfield.line: Kathleen O'Neal Gear got her bachelor's at Bakersfield, worked as a government archaeologist and historian in Wyoming, Kansas and Nebraska, then wrote novels good enough to win a lifetime achievement award in Western literature in twenty twenty one. That's digging in.

csu-bakersfield.name: Jeff Colson
csu-bakersfield.fact: Jeff Colson, B.A. in Fine Arts 1979, is an artist and recipient of the Guggenheim Fellowship.
csu-bakersfield.evidence: Jeff Colson, artist, recipient of the Guggenheim Fellowship – BA, Fine Arts 1979
csu-bakersfield.line: Jeff Colson, fine arts, class of seventy nine, went on to win a Guggenheim Fellowship as an artist. Folks forget Bakersfield makes artists too. We do.

csu-bakersfield.name: Jennifer L. Thurston
csu-bakersfield.fact: Jennifer L. Thurston, B.S. 1989, is a U.S. District Court judge for the Eastern District of California.
csu-bakersfield.evidence: Jennifer L. Thurston, U.S. District Court Judge, Eastern District of California – BS, 1989
csu-bakersfield.line: Jennifer Thurston, class of eighty nine, is a United States District Court judge for the Eastern District of California. A Roadrunner on the federal bench, and we're proud of it.

csu-bakersfield.name: Kevin McCarthy
csu-bakersfield.fact: Kevin McCarthy earned a B.S. in marketing in 1989 and an MBA in 1994 at CSU Bakersfield, became Speaker on the 15th ballot on January 7, 2023, and later that year became the first Speaker in U.S. history removed from office by the House.
csu-bakersfield.evidence: where he obtained a Bachelor of Science in marketing in 1989 and a Master of Business Administration in 1994. | McCarthy finally received a majority and became speaker on the 15th ballot on January 7 | This was the first time in U.S. history that the House of Representatives had removed its speaker from office. | On December 6, 2023, McCarthy announced that he would resign from Congress on December 31.
csu-bakersfield.line: Kevin McCarthy has two degrees from Bakersfield, one of them in marketing. He needed fifteen ballots to become Speaker, then became the first Speaker the House ever removed. Tough sell, even for a marketing man.

csu-bakersfield.name: Dushyant Chautala
csu-bakersfield.fact: Dushyant Chautala, B.S. in Business Administration 2014, is an Indian politician who has served as a Member of Parliament.
csu-bakersfield.evidence: Dushyant Chautala, Indian Politician, Member of Parliament – BS, Business Administration, 2014
csu-bakersfield.line: Here's one you might not know. Dushyant Chautala took a business degree from Bakersfield in twenty fourteen and went on to be a Member of Parliament in India. Roadrunners travel.

csun.name: Judy Baca
csun.known_for: muralist, Great Wall of Los Angeles
csun.fact: Judy Baca earned a bachelor's degree at CSUN in 1969 and a master's in fine art in 1979, and painted the first phase of the Great Wall of Los Angeles with more than 400 young people, artists and scholars over seven summers from 1976 to 1984.
csun.evidence: She then attended California State University, Northridge (CSUN) and earned her bachelor's degree in 1969 and a master's degree in fine art in 1979. | painted the first phase with more than 400 young people, artists, and scholars over seven summers from 1976 to 1984 | By the end of the project, the mural measured half a mile (0.80 km) in length
csun.line: Judy Baca, two CSUN degrees, painted the Great Wall of Los Angeles with more than four hundred young people, artists and scholars over seven summers. Half a mile of mural. That's a Matador thinking big.

csun.name: Lorraine Foster
csun.years: alumna; year not listed on source
csun.fact: Lorraine Foster, a mathematician on CSUN's alumni list, was the first woman to receive a Ph.D. in mathematics from the California Institute of Technology.
csun.evidence: Lorraine Foster– mathematician, first woman to receive a Ph.D. in mathematics from California Institute of Technology
csun.line: Lorraine Foster, Matador mathematician, was the first woman to receive a doctorate in math from Caltech. First one through the door. Respect.

csun.name: Mark! Lopez
csun.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
csun.fact: Mark! Lopez, on CSUN's alumni list, is an activist and winner of the Goldman Environmental Prize.
csun.evidence: Mark! Lopez– activist and winner of the Goldman Environmental Prize
csun.line: Mark Lopez, CSUN alum and activist, won the Goldman Environmental Prize. And yes, he spells his first name with an exclamation point. He earned it.

csun.name: Stephen Bollenbach
csun.fact: Stephen Bollenbach (1942-2016) earned a master's in management at CSUN in 1968, became the first CFO of the Trump Organization in 1990, and left Hilton in 2007 after selling it to The Blackstone Group for $26 billion.
csun.evidence: a master's degree in management from the California State University, Northridge in 1968. | Bollenbach became the first CFO of the Trump Organization in 1990 while Allen Weisselberg worked under him as comptroller. | In 2007, Bollenbach left after making the sale of Hilton to The Blackstone Group for $26 Billion. | Stephen Frasier Bollenbach (July 14, 1942 – October 8, 2016)
csun.line: Stephen Bollenbach took a CSUN master's in management and became the very first chief financial officer of the Trump Organization in nineteen ninety. Later he sold Hilton to Blackstone for twenty six billion dollars. Management, sure. We'll call it that.

csun.name: Diane Warren
csun.years: alumna; year not listed on source
csun.fact: Diane Warren, on CSUN's alumni list, is a musician and music publisher who has won a Grammy Award, an Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award.
csun.evidence: Diane Warren– musician, music publisher, winner of a Grammy Award, an Emmy Award, and a Golden Globe Award
csun.line: Diane Warren, Matador, has a Grammy, an Emmy and a Golden Globe on the shelf. The Valley writes the hits, everybody else just sings along.

davidson.name: Mary T. Martin Sloop
davidson.fact: Sloop attended Davidson College, earned her medical degree in 1906, and founded the Crossnore School in 1913.
davidson.evidence: "She pursued her college education from both Statesville Female College and Davidson College." "She ended up receiving her degree from the Women's Medical College of Pennsylvania at Philadelphia in 1906." "Sloop founded the Crossnore School in 1913 with her husband, Dr. Eustace H. Sloop." "Over the next 40 years, Sloop would build the one-room schoolhouse into a complex of twenty buildings and over 250 acres," "(March 9, 1873 – January 13, 1962)"
davidson.line: Behold, Doctor Mary Martin Sloop! She studied at Davidson, earned her medical degree in nineteen-oh-six, and in nineteen thirteen founded the Crossnore School, growing one room into twenty buildings. A standing ovation, if you please!

davidson.name: William Emerson
davidson.years: attended; left early to serve in World War II
davidson.fact: Emerson left Davidson early to serve in World War II and became a civil rights journalist for Newsweek and editor in chief of The Saturday Evening Post.
davidson.evidence: "William Emerson, civil rights journalist for Newsweek; editor in chief of The Saturday Evening Post;" ... "left Davidson early to serve in World War II."
davidson.line: William Emerson left Davidson early to serve in World War Two, then covered civil rights for Newsweek and rose to editor in chief of The Saturday Evening Post. Magnificent, I say!

davidson.name: Lunsford Richardson
davidson.fact: Richardson graduated from Davidson with highest honors in Latin in 1875 and introduced Vick's Magic Croup Salve in 1905; it was rebranded VapoRub in 1912.
davidson.evidence: "He attended Horner and Graves School and Davidson College, where he graduated with highest honors in Latin in 1875." "It was introduced in 1905 with the name Vick's Magic Croup Salve and rebranded as VapoRub in 1912 at the instigation of H. Smith Richardson." "Died: August 21, 1919 (aged 64)"
davidson.line: Step right up for Lunsford Richardson, class of eighteen seventy-five, highest honors in Latin! In nineteen-oh-five he introduced Vick's Magic Croup Salve, rebranded in nineteen twelve as VapoRub. Your sinuses salute him!

davidson.name: William Styron
davidson.fact: Styron attended Davidson in 1942 and left to join the Marines.
davidson.evidence: "William Styron, author; attended in 1942, left to join the Marines"
davidson.line: And the author William Styron graced our campus in nineteen forty-two, then departed to join the Marines. A brief engagement, ladies and gentlemen, but we shall claim him forever!

dayton.name: Erma Bombeck
dayton.fact: Bombeck graduated from Dayton in 1949 with an English degree; by 1978, 900 U.S. newspapers carried her column.
dayton.evidence: "Erma later enrolled in the University of Dayton, a Catholic college." "She graduated in 1949 with a degree in English" "By 1978, nine hundred U.S. newspapers were publishing Bombeck's column." "her columns were read semi-weekly by 30 million readers" "Erma Louise Bombeck (née Fiste; February 21, 1927 – April 22, 1996)"
dayton.line: Erma Bombeck, class of nineteen forty-nine, English degree. By nineteen seventy-eight, nine hundred newspapers carried her column, reaching thirty million readers. That is a Flyer in very high orbit.

dayton.name: Jessie Scott Hathcock
dayton.fact: Hathcock, class of 1930, was the University of Dayton's first female African American graduate.
dayton.evidence: "Jessie Scott Hathcock'30 - first female African American graduate; humanitarian, educator, and civil rights leader"
dayton.line: Jessie Scott Hathcock, class of nineteen thirty, the first African American woman to graduate from Dayton. Educator, humanitarian, civil rights leader. Mission accomplished, and then some.

dayton.name: Charles J. Pedersen
dayton.fact: Pedersen, class of 1926, won the 1987 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
dayton.evidence: "Charles J. Pedersen'26 - winner of 1987 Nobel Prize in Chemistry"
dayton.line: Charles Pedersen, class of nineteen twenty-six, winner of the nineteen eighty-seven Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Flight confirms: that is a Flyer on the biggest podium in science.

dayton.name: David J. Bradley
dayton.fact: Bradley earned a bachelor's in electrical engineering from Dayton in 1971 and in 1980 was one of twelve engineers developing the first IBM Personal Computer.
dayton.evidence: "Bachelors, Electrical Engineering, University of Dayton (Ohio), 1971." "In 1980, Bradley was one of twelve engineers developing the first IBM Personal Computer." "David J. Bradley'71 - inventor of the "Control-Alt-Delete" computer keyboard command" (list page) "David J. Bradley (born 4 January 1949) is one of the twelve engineers who worked on the original"
dayton.line: David Bradley, electrical engineering, class of seventy-one, was one of twelve engineers on the first IBM personal computer, and he gave us Control-Alt-Delete. When all systems fail, you reboot with a Flyer.

dayton.name: Joseph Desch
dayton.fact: Desch, class of 1926, created a decoding machine to crack the Nazi Enigma code in World War II.
dayton.evidence: "Joseph Desch'26 - creator of decoding machine to crack Nazi Enigma code in World War II"
dayton.line: Joseph Desch, class of nineteen twenty-six, created a decoding machine to crack the Nazi Enigma code in World War Two. Quiet work. Enormous payload.

detroit-mercy.name: Elmore Leonard
detroit-mercy.fact: Elmore Leonard enrolled at the University of Detroit in 1946 on the G.I. Bill and graduated in 1950 with a bachelor's degree in English and philosophy.
detroit-mercy.evidence: Enrolling at the University of Detroit in 1946, on the G.I. Bill ... He graduated in 1950 with a bachelor's degree in English and philosophy. ... he got a job as a copy writer with Campbell-Ewald Advertising Agency ... Get Shorty was adapted into an eponymous film in 1995 ... Rum Punch was adapted as the Quentin Tarantino film Jackie Brown (1997) ... Elmore John Leonard Jr. (October 11, 1925 – August 20, 2013)
detroit-mercy.line: Elmore Leonard came here on the G.I. Bill and graduated in 1950, English and philosophy. He wrote ad copy, then wrote the books behind Get Shorty and Jackie Brown. Detroit taught him to keep it short.

detroit-mercy.name: Richard Arrington Jr.
detroit-mercy.fact: Richard Arrington Jr., listed among University of Detroit Mercy people, was the first African-American mayor of Birmingham, Alabama.
detroit-mercy.evidence: [From the page that opens: The following is a list of notable people associated with the University of Detroit Mercy.] Richard Arrington, Jr., first African-American mayor of Birmingham, Alabama
detroit-mercy.line: Richard Arrington Junior is one of ours. First African-American mayor of Birmingham, Alabama. Birmingham. Think about what that took, then tell me your Tuesday was hard.

detroit-mercy.name: Kyra Harris Bolden
detroit-mercy.fact: Kyra Harris Bolden, listed among University of Detroit Mercy people, is a justice of the Michigan Supreme Court.
detroit-mercy.evidence: [From the page that opens: The following is a list of notable people associated with the University of Detroit Mercy.] Kyra Harris Bolden, justice of the Michigan Supreme Court
detroit-mercy.line: Kyra Harris Bolden, Detroit Mercy, now a justice of the Michigan Supreme Court. When a Titan says she'll see you in court, she means the top one.

detroit-mercy.name: Keegan-Michael Key
detroit-mercy.fact: Keegan-Michael Key, an actor, is listed among University of Detroit Mercy people.
detroit-mercy.evidence: [From the page that opens: The following is a list of notable people associated with the University of Detroit Mercy.] Keegan-Michael Key, actor
detroit-mercy.line: Keegan-Michael Key, the actor, is a Titan. So yes, somebody from this school gets paid to be funny on purpose.

detroit-mercy.name: Glynn Lunney
detroit-mercy.fact: Glynn Lunney, listed among University of Detroit Mercy people, was a NASA flight director.
detroit-mercy.evidence: [From the page that opens: The following is a list of notable people associated with the University of Detroit Mercy.] Glynn Lunney, NASA flight director
detroit-mercy.line: Glynn Lunney went from Detroit to NASA flight director. The Motor City builds things that move. Sometimes they leave the planet.

drake.name: Susan Glaspell
drake.years: enrolled at age 21; graduation year not given on source
drake.fact: Enrolled at Drake at twenty-one, founded the Provincetown Players with her husband, and was awarded the Pulitzer Prize in 1931 for the play Alison's House.
drake.evidence: At twenty-one, Glaspell enrolled at Drake University... | With her husband George Cram Cook, she founded the Provincetown Players, the first modern American theatre company. | She also wrote the play Alison's House (1930), for which she was awarded the Pulitzer Prize in 1931. | Susan Keating Glaspell (July 1, 1876 – July 28, 1948) was an American playwright, novelist, journalist and actress.
drake.line: Susan Glaspell enrolled at Drake at twenty-one, darling, then helped found the Provincetown Players, the first modern American theatre company. In 1931 she collected a Pulitzer for her play Alison's House. Now that is an encore.

drake.name: Roxanne Conlin
drake.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
drake.fact: Served as U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Iowa from 1977 to 1981.
drake.evidence: Roxanne Conlin, lawyer, former U.S. attorney for the Southern District of Iowa (1977–1981), and Iowa senate…
drake.line: Roxanne Conlin, Drake alumna and lawyer, was the United States attorney for the Southern District of Iowa from 1977 to 1981. A Bulldog with a badge, and I adore it.

drake.name: Brian Wansink
drake.years: M.A. in journalism and mass communication, 1984
drake.known_for: food researcher found to have committed misconduct
drake.fact: Cornell determined on September 20, 2018 that he had committed scientific misconduct; he resigned effective June 30, 2019.
drake.evidence: ...and an M.A. in journalism and mass communication from Drake University in 1984... | On September 20, 2018, Cornell determined that Wansink had committed scientific misconduct... | He also resigned from the university, effective June 30, 2019. | In 2006, Wansink published Mindless Eating: Why We Eat More Than We Think.
drake.line: Brian Wansink, Drake master's, 1984, wrote a book called Mindless Eating. Then in 2018 Cornell determined he had committed scientific misconduct, and he resigned. We claim him, darling, but quietly, over by the punch bowl.

drake.name: Steve Allen
drake.known_for: first host of The Tonight Show
drake.fact: Attended Drake without graduating and became the first host of The Tonight Show.
drake.evidence: Steve Allen, comedian, actor and first host of The Tonight Show (attended, did not graduate)
drake.line: Steve Allen attended Drake, did not stay for the diploma, and went on to be the very first host of The Tonight Show. Some people simply cannot wait for the party to start.

drake.name: Harley A. Wilhelm
drake.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
drake.fact: Manhattan Project scientist and co-inventor of the Ames Process for purifying uranium.
drake.evidence: Harley A. Wilhelm, Manhattan Project scientist and co-inventor of the Ames Process for purifying uranium,…
drake.line: Drake's Harley Wilhelm was a Manhattan Project scientist who co-invented the Ames Process for purifying uranium. Rather heavier than bathtub gin, darling.

duquesne.name: Derrick Bell
duquesne.fact: Bell earned his bachelor's degree at Duquesne in 1952 and later supervised more than 300 school desegregation cases.
duquesne.evidence: "choosing to attend Duquesne University instead" "graduated with his bachelor's degree in 1952" "Bell supervised more than 300 school desegregation cases" "He resigned from his position at Harvard in protest of the school's hiring procedures." "Derrick Albert Bell Jr. (November 6, 1930 – October 5, 2011)"
duquesne.line: Derrick Bell, Duquesne class of nineteen fifty-two, supervised more than three hundred school desegregation cases, then resigned from Harvard in protest of its hiring. One does admire a gentleman of principle.

duquesne.name: Joseph M. Gaydos
duquesne.fact: Gaydos, class of 1947, was the first Slovak-American elected to Congress.
duquesne.evidence: "Joseph M. Gaydos(1947)– Pennsylvania delegate to U.S. House of Representatives; first Slovak-American elected to Congress"
duquesne.line: Joseph Gaydos, class of nineteen forty-seven, represented Pennsylvania in the House and was the first Slovak-American elected to Congress. From Duquesne to the Capitol. Splendid.

duquesne.name: Mark Ciavarella
duquesne.fact: Ciavarella received his J.D. from Duquesne in 1975; a federal jury convicted him in 2011 and he was sentenced to 28 years. A racketeering conviction was later thrown out; the fraud convictions stood.
duquesne.evidence: "After graduating from the local King's College he attended Duquesne University School of Law," "receiving his J.D. degree in 1975." "On February 18, 2011, a jury in federal court found Ciavarella guilty of racketeering." "On August 11, 2011, Kosik sentenced Ciavarella to 28 years in federal prison." "Mark Ciavarella– disbarred former Luzerne County judge following the kids for cash scandal" (list page)
duquesne.line: We must, regrettably, acknowledge Mark Ciavarella, Duquesne Law, nineteen seventy-five. A federal jury convicted the former judge in twenty eleven, and he was sentenced to twenty-eight years. A racketeering conviction was later thrown out, the fraud convictions stood. Hardly our finest export.

duquesne.name: Werner Herzog
duquesne.fact: The filmmaker Werner Herzog is listed among Duquesne's people with the note that he did not officially graduate.
duquesne.evidence: "Werner Herzog– filmmaker (did not officially graduate)" (list intro: "This is a list of notable persons affiliated with Duquesne University, including alumni, current and former faculty members")
duquesne.line: The filmmaker Werner Herzog appears on our rolls, though, one must confess, he did not officially graduate. We claim him regardless. It is the aristocratic thing to do.

duquesne.name: Bobby Vinton
duquesne.fact: Vinton graduated from Duquesne in 1956 and received an honorary doctorate in music in 1978.
duquesne.evidence: "(graduated 1956; honorary doctorate in Music in 1978) – "the Polish Prince," recording artist, called most successful love singer of rock era"
duquesne.line: Bobby Vinton, the Polish Prince, graduated in nineteen fifty-six and collected an honorary doctorate in music in nineteen seventy-eight. A prince among Dukes. How very fitting.

eastern-michigan.name: Andrew Foster
eastern-michigan.fact: Foster earned a master's degree in education from Eastern Michigan in 1955 and went on to establish 32 churches and mission schools for the Deaf in thirteen African nations.
eastern-michigan.evidence: one in education from Eastern Michigan University in 1955 | In 1954, he became the first Deaf African American to earn a bachelor's degree from Gallaudet University | In 1956, upon learning that there were only 12 deaf schools in the whole continent of Africa | Overall, Foster established 32 churches and mission schools for the Deaf in thirteen nations across Africa. | Andrew Foster died on December 3, 1987
eastern-michigan.line: Andrew Foster earned his master's in education here in 1955. A year later he learned Africa had only twelve schools for the deaf, so he went and established thirty-two churches and mission schools in thirteen nations. That is a teacher.

eastern-michigan.name: Vallateen Virginia Dudley Abbington
eastern-michigan.years: attended Michigan State Normal College; years not given
eastern-michigan.fact: Abbington was the plaintiff in the 1940 case Abbington v. Board of Education of Louisville, brought when Black teachers earned from $1,490 while white teachers earned $1,750; the board equalized pay in 1941.
eastern-michigan.evidence: She attended Michigan State Normal College, where she joined the sorority Alpha Kappa Alpha. | to bring the issue to court in the 1940 case Abbington v. Board of Education of Louisville. | as Abbington and other African American teachers earned from $1,490 while white teachers earned $1,750. | the school board informed Abbington that they would provide equal pay for all if she dropped her case against them [...] which they did in 1941. || EMU list page: Vallateen Virginia Dudley Abbington – African-American activist, educator, and social worker known for being the plaintiff in Abbington v. Board of Education of Louisville
eastern-michigan.line: Vallateen Abbington was a teacher in Louisville when Black teachers earned from 1,490 dollars and white teachers 1,750. In 1940 she took the school board to court. By 1941 the board had agreed to equal pay. One of ours.

eastern-michigan.name: Kevin Saunderson
eastern-michigan.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
eastern-michigan.fact: Kevin Saunderson is a DJ and producer and one of The Belleville Three, pioneers of Detroit techno.
eastern-michigan.evidence: Kevin Saunderson – DJ and producer, one of The Belleville Three, pioneers of Detroit techno
eastern-michigan.line: Kevin Saunderson is a D J and producer, one of the Belleville Three, the pioneers of Detroit techno. So if the arena music has a beat tonight, you may thank an Eagle.

eastern-michigan.name: John Harvey Kellogg
eastern-michigan.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
eastern-michigan.fact: John Harvey Kellogg took a teacher's training course at Michigan State Normal School, now Eastern Michigan; his is the only name on the corn flakes patent.
eastern-michigan.evidence: John Harvey Kellogg – co-founder of the Kellogg Company; co-creator of corn flakes
eastern-michigan.line: John Harvey Kellogg took a teacher's training course at Michigan State Normal School, now Eastern Michigan, and his is the only name on the corn flakes patent. Breakfast, class. It started with one of ours.

evansville.name: Lisel Mueller
evansville.fact: Arrived in the U.S. in 1939 at age 15 after her family fled the Nazi regime, graduated from Evansville in 1944, and won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry in 1997.
evansville.evidence: She graduated from the University of Evansville in 1944. | Her family fled the Nazi regime, and she arrived in the U.S. in 1939 at the age of 15. | She received awards including the National Book Award in 1981 and the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry in 1997… | Lisel Mueller (born Elisabeth Neumann, February 8, 1924 – February 21, 2020)
evansville.line: Lisel Mueller's family fled the Nazi regime, and she arrived in America at fifteen. She graduated from Evansville in 1944 and won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry in 1997. The crown bows to no one, yet it bows to her.

evansville.name: Culla Johnson Vayhinger
evansville.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
evansville.fact: Culla Johnson Vayhinger (1867–1924) was president of the Woman's Christian Temperance Union of Indiana.
evansville.evidence: Culla Johnson Vayhinger (1867–1924), President, Woman's Christian Temperance Union of Indiana
evansville.line: Culla Johnson Vayhinger, born 1867, rose to lead the Woman's Christian Temperance Union of Indiana as its president. A reformer of iron will, and one of ours.

evansville.name: Ron Glass
evansville.years: attended after 1964; degree year not given on source
evansville.fact: Attended Evansville after graduating from St. Francis Seminary in 1964, played Detective Ron Harris on Barney Miller from 1975 to 1982, and later received the university's Medal of Honor.
evansville.evidence: After graduating from St. Francis Seminary in 1964, Glass attended the University of Evansville... | He was known for his roles as literary Detective Ron Harris in the television sitcom Barney Miller (1975–1982)... | Years later, the university awarded him its Medal of Honor. | Ronald Earle Glass (July 10, 1945 – November 25, 2016) was an American actor.
evansville.line: Ron Glass attended Evansville, then played Detective Ron Harris on Barney Miller from 1975 to 1982. Years later the university awarded him its Medal of Honor. The crown approves.

evansville.name: Rami Malek
evansville.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
evansville.fact: Academy Award-winning actor whose credits include Mr. Robot and The Pacific.
evansville.evidence: Rami Malek, Academy Award-winning actor The Pacific, Night at the Museum, The War at Home, Mr. Robot and Bohemian Rha...
evansville.line: Rami Malek, of The Pacific and Mr. Robot, is an Academy Award-winning actor and a Purple Ace. One does enjoy having an Oscar in the royal household.

evansville.name: Jack McBrayer
evansville.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
evansville.fact: Actor known for 30 Rock and Forgetting Sarah Marshall.
evansville.evidence: Jack McBrayer, actor 30 Rock, Forgetting Sarah Marshall
evansville.line: Jack McBrayer of 30 Rock and Forgetting Sarah Marshall studied at Evansville. Every court requires a jester, and ours is splendid.

fairfield.name: Liz Wahl
fairfield.known_for: quit Russian state TV on air
fairfield.fact: Wahl, a Fairfield graduate, resigned on live television from the Russian government-sponsored network RT on March 5, 2014.
fairfield.evidence: "Liz Wahl (2008) – former Russia Today news anchor who quit on air for ethical reasons" [List_of_Fairfield_University_alumni entry] ... "She graduated from Fairfield University." ... "On March 5, 2014, Wahl went off script and resigned her job during her live segment while denouncing her employer RT."
fairfield.line: Liz Wahl, class of two thousand eight, was anchoring for the Russian government's RT network when, in March of twenty fourteen, she went off script and quit live on air. That is how you resign, Stags.

fairfield.name: Peter Pronovost
fairfield.fact: Pronovost, class of 1984, was named a MacArthur Fellow in 2008 and one of Time magazine's 100 most influential people.
fairfield.evidence: "Peter Pronovost (1984) – 2008 MacArthur Fellow and one of Time magazine's 100 World's Most Influential People"
fairfield.line: Peter Pronovost, class of eighty-four: a MacArthur Fellow in two thousand eight and one of Time magazine's hundred most influential people in the world. Quick, polished, brilliant. Very Fairfield.

fairfield.name: Caitlin O'Connell-Rodwell
fairfield.fact: O'Connell-Rodwell, class of 1987, is an elephant expert and an instructor at Stanford University Medical School.
fairfield.evidence: "Caitlin O'Connell-Rodwell (1987) – world renowned elephant expert; instructor at Stanford University Medical School"
fairfield.line: Caitlin O'Connell-Rodwell, class of eighty-seven, is a world renowned elephant expert who teaches at Stanford's medical school. A Stag who studies elephants. I love this job.

fairfield.name: Githa Hariharan
fairfield.fact: Hariharan, class of 1977, is a Commonwealth Writers' Prize-winning author and editor.
fairfield.evidence: "Githa Hariharan (1977) – Commonwealth Writers' Prize-winning author and editor"
fairfield.line: Githa Hariharan, class of seventy-seven, is a Commonwealth Writers' Prize-winning author and editor. Add her to your reading list, Stags. Quickly.

fairfield.name: Joseph Berardino
fairfield.fact: Berardino was chief executive of Arthur Andersen when its client Enron went bankrupt; he resigned on March 26, 2002, and by the end of August the firm had surrendered its licenses to audit public companies.
fairfield.evidence: "Joseph Berardino (1972) – managing director, Alvarez & Marsal; former CEO, Arthur Andersen" [List_of_Fairfield_University_alumni entry] ... "after graduating from the Fairfield University Dolan School of Business with a B.S. in accounting." ... "Berardino became managing partner – chief executive officer of Andersen Worldwide" ... "When Andersen's client Enron declared bankruptcy in the highly publicized Enron scandal," ... "He resigned on March 26, 2002, in the hope that justice would reconsider the indictment." ... "By the end of August, it surrendered its licenses to audit public companies in the US."
fairfield.line: Joe Berardino, accounting degree, class of seventy-two, was running Arthur Andersen when its client Enron went bankrupt. He resigned in March of two thousand two, and by the end of August the firm had surrendered its audit licenses. We claim him, Stags. Carefully.

fgcu.name: Cherie DeVaux
fgcu.fact: DeVaux, who attended FGCU, won the 2024 Breeders' Cup Mile as a trainer and became the first woman to train a Kentucky Derby winner.
fgcu.evidence: "She attended Lemon Bay High School and Florida Gulf Coast University" ... "becoming the first woman to train a Derby winner." ... "She is the second woman trainer to win the Belmont." ... "winning the 2024 Breeders' Cup Mile"
fgcu.line: Cherie DeVaux attended FGCU, then became the first woman ever to train a Kentucky Derby winner. She is also only the second woman trainer to win the Belmont. Eagles fly, and apparently they gallop too!

fgcu.name: Priscila Navarro
fgcu.fact: Navarro, born in 1994 in Huánuco, Peru, studied at FGCU's Bower School of Music and won first place at the 2013 Biennial International Beethoven Sonata Competition.
fgcu.evidence: "As of 2014, Navarro was enrolled at the Bower School of Music at Florida Gulf Coast University." ... "Priscila Navarro (born 27 April 1994, in Huánuco) is a Peruvian pianist." ... "2013: First place Biennial International Beethoven Sonata Competition"
fgcu.line: Priscila Navarro, no relation, I wish, came from Huánuco, Peru to study piano at FGCU's Bower School of Music. In twenty thirteen she took first place at the International Beethoven Sonata Competition. Dunk City has a concert hall side.

fgcu.name: Ross Chastain
fgcu.years: listed among FGCU notable people; year not shown
fgcu.fact: Chastain is a professional racecar driver listed among FGCU's notable people.
fgcu.line: Ross Chastain is on the FGCU list as a professional racecar driver. So yes, we do have somebody faster than our fast break.

fgcu.name: Courtney Jolly
fgcu.years: listed among FGCU notable people; year not shown
fgcu.fact: Jolly earned a marketing degree at FGCU and drove monster trucks professionally until 2008.
fgcu.line: Courtney Jolly earned her marketing degree at FGCU and drove monster trucks professionally while she was still in school. Some schools produce senators. We produced a woman who drove over cars for a living, and honestly, I prefer ours.

fordham.name: Eunice Carter
fordham.fact: In 1932 Carter became the first Black woman to receive a Fordham law degree, and in 1935 the first Black woman assistant district attorney in New York State.
fordham.evidence: "In 1932, Carter became the first black woman to receive a law degree from Fordham University in New York City." "In 1935 Carter became the first black woman assistant district attorney in the state of New York." "Carter then put together a massive prostitution racketeering case that eventually implicated Luciano." "Died: January 25, 1970 (aged 72) New York City, US"
fordham.line: In nineteen thirty-two, Eunice Carter became the first Black woman to earn a Fordham law degree. Three years later, New York's first Black woman assistant district attorney. Then she built the case that implicated Lucky Luciano. Olé.

fordham.name: Susan Love
fordham.fact: Love, B.S. 1970, was a surgeon and co-founder of the National Breast Cancer Coalition.
fordham.evidence: "| Susan Love | 1970 | FC | B.S. | Surgeon, co-founder of National Breast Cancer Coalition |  |"
fordham.line: Susan Love. Class of nineteen seventy. Surgeon. Co-founder of the National Breast Cancer Coalition. She chose the fight that matters.

fordham.name: Angelo Mozilo
fordham.fact: Mozilo, co-founder and CEO of Countrywide Financial, agreed to pay $67.5 million in fines and accepted a lifetime ban to settle SEC charges.
fordham.evidence: "He was a graduate of Fordham University." "| Angelo Mozilo | 1960 | CBA |  | Co-founder, chairman, and CEO of Countrywide Financial Corporation |  |" (list page) "Mozilo agreed to pay $67.5 million in fines, and accepted a lifetime ban" "The company's status as a major lender of subprime mortgages made it a central player in a subsequent mortgage crisis." "where he died on July 16, 2023, at age 84, of natural causes."
fordham.line: Angelo Mozilo, class of nineteen sixty, co-founded Countrywide, a central player in the mortgage crisis. He agreed to pay sixty-seven and a half million dollars in fines and took a lifetime ban. Fordham claims him. Quietly.

fordham.name: Denzel Washington
fordham.fact: Washington, B.A. 1977, is an Academy Award, Golden Globe and Tony-winning actor.
fordham.evidence: "| Denzel Washington | 1977 | FC | B.A. | Academy Award, Golden Globe, and Tony-winning actor |  |"
fordham.line: Denzel Washington. Class of nineteen seventy-seven. An Academy Award. A Golden Globe. A Tony. The ring belongs to him.

fordham.name: Lana Del Rey
fordham.fact: Lana Del Rey, B.A. 2008, is a BRIT Award-winning and Grammy-nominated singer and songwriter.
fordham.evidence: "| Lana Del Rey | 2008 | FC | B.A. | BRIT Award-winning and Grammy-nominated singer and songwriter |  |"
fordham.line: Lana Del Rey. Class of two thousand eight. BRIT Award winner, Grammy nominee. Even the melancholy is a Ram.

george-mason.name: Zainab Salbi
george-mason.fact: Salbi, a George Mason alumna, is the former president of Women for Women International.
george-mason.evidence: Listed under the heading "Notable George Mason University alumni Include:" as "Zainab Salbi, former president of Women for Women International"
george-mason.line: Oh, I love this one! Mason alumna Zainab Salbi was president of Women for Women International. Women, for women, internationally. That is a triple axel of good!

george-mason.name: Charniele Herring
george-mason.fact: Herring, a George Mason alumna, is Majority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates.
george-mason.evidence: Listed under the heading "Notable George Mason University alumni Include:" as "Charniele Herring, Majority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates"
george-mason.line: Patriots, meet Charniele Herring, Mason alumna and Majority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates. Majority Leader! Yes, I am giggling with pride!

george-mason.name: Christine Fox
george-mason.fact: Fox, a George Mason alumna, is a former acting U.S. Deputy Secretary of Defense.
george-mason.evidence: Listed under the heading "Notable George Mason University alumni Include:" as "Christine Fox, former acting U.S. Deputy Secretary of Defense"
george-mason.line: Christine Fox, a Mason alumna, served as acting Deputy Secretary of Defense for the whole United States. Sparkle, sparkle, salute!

george-mason.name: Karl Rove
george-mason.fact: Rove attended George Mason without earning a degree and resigned from the White House on August 31, 2007.
george-mason.evidence: "University of Utah (attended) George Mason University (attended)" "he did not have a degree because "I lack at this point one math class, which I can take by exam, and my foreign language requirement."" "until his resignation on August 31, 2007." "The Committee concluded that Rove had played a significant role in the Attorney firings." "Karl Christian Rove (born December 25, 1950)"
george-mason.line: Okay, deep breath! Karl Rove attended Mason and by his own account never finished a degree. He resigned from the White House in two thousand seven, and a House committee concluded he played a significant role in the attorney firings. Moving on!

george-mason.name: Archie Kao
george-mason.fact: Kao, an actor, is listed among George Mason's notable alumni.
george-mason.evidence: Listed under the heading "Notable George Mason University alumni Include:" as "Archie Kao, actor"
george-mason.line: And for the showbiz fans, the actor Archie Kao is a Mason alum too. Lights, camera, Patriots!

george-washington.name: Peggy Cooper Cafritz
george-washington.fact: Cafritz received her J.D. from GW Law in 1971 and helped open the Duke Ellington School of the Arts in 1974.
george-washington.evidence: "to attend George Washington University (GW)" "Cafritz went on to attend George Washington University Law School, and received her J.D. degree in 1971."
