"worked successfully for the integration of fraternities and sororities." "opening the public magnet school Duke Ellington School of the Arts in Georgetown in 1974." "April 7, 1947 – February 18, 2018"
george-washington.line: Hear this! Peggy Cooper Cafritz worked to integrate the fraternities and sororities at this very university, took her law degree in nineteen seventy-one, and helped open the Duke Ellington School of the Arts in nineteen seventy-four. A revolutionary indeed!

george-washington.name: Ellen Malcolm
george-washington.fact: Malcolm, a GW alumna, is the founder and president of EMILYs List.
george-washington.evidence: "Ellen Malcolm, founder and president of EMILYs List" (from the page List of George Washington University alumni)
george-washington.line: I give you Ellen Malcolm, alumna of this university, founder and president of EMILYs List. Some raise armies, my friends. She raised a movement.

george-washington.name: Mildred Harnack
george-washington.fact: Harnack, a GW alumna, was a resistance fighter in Nazi Germany who was beheaded by the Gestapo.
george-washington.evidence: "Mildred Harnack, resistance fighter in Nazi Germany who was beheaded by the Gestapo" (from the page List of George Washington University alumni)
george-washington.line: Let the record show the name Mildred Harnack, of this university. A resistance fighter in Nazi Germany, beheaded by the Gestapo. Courage, my friends, of the highest order.

george-washington.name: Aldrich Ames
george-washington.years: bachelor's in history (year not given on page)
george-washington.fact: Ames completed a GW bachelor's degree in history, was convicted of espionage in 1994 after pleading guilty, and received $4.6 million from the Soviets.
george-washington.evidence: "Ames completed a bachelor's degree in history at the George Washington University in Washington, D.C." "convicted of espionage on behalf of the Soviet Union and Russia in 1994." "Ames pleaded guilty, and on April 28 U.S. district judge Claude M. Hilton sentenced him to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole." "Ultimately, Ames received $4.6 million (equivalent to $13.8 million in 2025) from the Soviets" "On January 5, 2026, Ames died at the Federal Correctional Institution, Cumberland, at the age of 84."
george-washington.line: And, with some reluctance, Aldrich Ames, bachelor's in history. He took four point six million dollars from the Soviets, pleaded guilty to espionage in nineteen ninety-four, and received life without parole. Benedict Arnold sends his regards.

george-washington.name: Kevin Peter Hall
george-washington.fact: Hall, a GW alumnus, was an actor known for Predator.
george-washington.evidence: "Kevin Peter Hall, actor, Predator" (from the page List of George Washington University alumni)
george-washington.line: On a lighter note, citizens, the actor Kevin Peter Hall, of Predator fame, is an alumnus of this institution. Even our monsters are well educated.

grand-canyon.name: Kevin Warren
grand-canyon.fact: Kevin Warren earned a business administration degree from Grand Canyon in 1986 and in 2015 became the first African-American chief operating officer of an NFL team.
grand-canyon.evidence: "where he earned his undergraduate degree in Business Administration in 1986." ... "Warren became the first African-American chief operating officer (COO) of an NFL team." ... "was the first African-American leader of the Big Ten." ... "He is the team president and chief executive officer (CEO) for the Chicago Bears."
grand-canyon.line: Kevin Warren got his business degree right here in 1986. Then he became the first African-American chief operating officer of an NFL team and the first African-American leader of the Big Ten. That is a Lope running the room, Phoenix!

green-bay.name: Barbara Lawton
green-bay.known_for: first woman elected Wisconsin lieutenant governor
green-bay.fact: Barbara Lawton, a UW-Green Bay student in 1973, became the first woman elected lieutenant governor of Wisconsin in 2002 and served from 2003 to 2011.
green-bay.evidence: She met and married Charles "Cal" Lawton in 1973 when she was a student at the University of Wisconsin–Green Bay. ... She became the first woman elected to the position in 2002 ... In office January 6, 2003 – January 3, 2011 ... Barbara Lawton (born July 5, 1951) [Green Bay page entry: Barbara Lawton, Lieutenant Governor of Wisconsin (attended)]
green-bay.line: Barbara Lawton was a student here back in 1973. In 2002 she became the first woman ever elected lieutenant governor of Wisconsin. Took the state long enough, but hey, a Phoenix got it done.

green-bay.name: Tony Shalhoub
green-bay.fact: Green Bay native Tony Shalhoub spent a short time at UW-Green Bay before transferring, and later won three Primetime Emmy Awards for Monk.
green-bay.evidence: Shalhoub was born and raised in a Lebanese Christian household in Green Bay, Wisconsin. ... After graduating from Green Bay East High School, he spent a short time at the University of Wisconsin–Green Bay before participating in the National Student Exchange to the University of Southern Maine where he later transferred and earned a bachelor's degree. ... He later starred as Adrian Monk in the USA Network series Monk (2002–2009), winning three Primetime Emmy Awards
green-bay.line: Tony Shalhoub grew up right here in Green Bay and spent a short time on our campus before he transferred out. Then he won three Emmys playing Monk. We had him first, we just didn't keep him tidy.

green-bay.name: Kevin MacLeod
green-bay.fact: Kevin MacLeod, a composer and music producer, attended UW-Green Bay but did not graduate.
green-bay.evidence: Kevin MacLeod, composer and music producer (did not graduate)
green-bay.line: Kevin MacLeod, composer and music producer, came through Green Bay and left without the diploma. That's okay, Kevin. The music turned out fine.

green-bay.name: Mike Grell
green-bay.fact: Mike Grell, a comic book writer and artist, is listed among UW-Green Bay's notable alumni.
green-bay.evidence: Mike Grell, comic book writer and artist
green-bay.line: Mike Grell, comic book writer and artist, is one of ours. He writes them and he draws them, so up here we call that a double double.

green-bay.name: Mark King
green-bay.fact: Mark King, listed among UW-Green Bay's notable alumni, is CEO of Taco Bell and former president and CEO of TaylorMade.
green-bay.evidence: Mark King, CEO of Taco Bell and former president & CEO of TaylorMade.
green-bay.line: Mark King ran TaylorMade, the golf outfit, and then became CEO of Taco Bell. From the fairway to the drive-through. Either way, you betcha, somebody's yelling fore.

hawaii.name: Alice Ball
hawaii.fact: In 1915 Alice Ball became the first woman and first Black American to earn a master's degree from the College of Hawaii; she died in 1916 at age 24.
hawaii.evidence: "In 1915 she became the first woman and first Black American to graduate with a master's degree from the College of Hawaii." ... "Ball died on December 31, 1916, at age 24." ... "In 2007, the University Board of Regents honored Ball with a Medal of Distinction, the school's highest honor." List entry: "M.S. in Chemistry, 1915" "chemist"
hawaii.line: In 1915, chemist Alice Ball became the first woman and the first Black American to earn a master's degree here. She died at just twenty-four. In 2007 the regents gave her the Medal of Distinction, our highest honor. Took us a while. She earned it.

hawaii.name: Patsy Mink
hawaii.fact: Patsy Mink earned bachelor's degrees in zoology and chemistry from the University of Hawaii in 1948 and co-authored the Title IX Amendment in 1972.
hawaii.evidence: "In 1948, she earned bachelor's degrees in zoology and chemistry from the university." ... "She was the first Woman of Color and first Asian-American woman elected to Congress" ... "In 1972, she co-authored the Title IX Amendment of the Higher Education Act" ... "renamed the Patsy T. Mink Equal Opportunity in Education Act in 2002."
hawaii.line: Patsy Mink, class of 1948, zoology and chemistry. First woman of color elected to Congress, and in 1972 she co-authored Title Nine. Every Rainbow Wahine team that takes the floor, that's Patsy's doing. Mahalo, Patsy.

hawaii.name: Ah Quon McElrath
hawaii.fact: Ah Quon McElrath (1915-2008) is listed among University of Hawaii alumni as a labor rights activist.
hawaii.evidence: List entry: Ah Quon McElrath (1915–2008), "labor rights activist"
hawaii.line: Ah Quon McElrath, born 1915, one of ours, spent her life as a labor rights activist. In these islands, somebody had to speak up for the working folks. She did.

hawaii.name: Tammy Duckworth
hawaii.fact: Tammy Duckworth earned a B.A. in political science from the University of Hawaii in 1990 and is a decorated war veteran and U.S. senator.
hawaii.evidence: List entry: "1990, B.A. political science" "decorated war veteran, U.S. senator"
hawaii.line: Tammy Duckworth, class of 1990, political science. Decorated war veteran, United States senator. Not bad for a kid who went to class up in the valley with the rest of us.

hawaii.name: Gordon Cooper
hawaii.fact: Astronaut Gordon Cooper attended the University of Hawaii but did not graduate.
hawaii.evidence: List entry: Gordon Cooper, "Attended, did not graduate", "astronaut"
hawaii.line: Gordon Cooper attended UH but never graduated. He became an astronaut instead. So if you're skipping class today, brah, you better have a rocket.

illinois-state.name: Donald McHenry
illinois-state.known_for: U.S. ambassador to the United Nations
illinois-state.fact: Class of 1957; served as U.S. ambassador to the United Nations from 1979 to 1981, during the Carter administration.
illinois-state.evidence: Donald McHenry, 1957, U.S. ambassador to the United Nations during the Carter Administration; Distinguished Professor of... | Donald McHenry– former U.S. ambassador to the United Nations(1979–81)
illinois-state.line: Donald McHenry, Redbird class of 1957, was the United States ambassador to the United Nations from 1979 to 1981, under President Carter. That is a perfect score for diplomacy.

illinois-state.name: Reg Weaver
illinois-state.fact: Class of 1962; president of the National Education Association from 2002 to 2008.
illinois-state.evidence: Reg Weaver, 1962, President of National Education Association 2002–2008
illinois-state.line: Reg Weaver, class of 1962, led the National Education Association as president from 2002 to 2008. Illinois State was built to make teachers, and he stood up for all of them.

illinois-state.name: Mboka Mwilambwe
illinois-state.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
illinois-state.fact: First African-American mayor of Bloomington, Illinois.
illinois-state.evidence: Mboka Mwilambwe– first African-American mayor of Bloomington, Illinois
illinois-state.line: Mboka Mwilambwe, a Redbird, became the first African-American mayor of Bloomington, Illinois. A first-place finish, right in our own backyard.

illinois-state.name: Laurie Metcalf
illinois-state.fact: Class of 1976; one of six actors to win Tony Awards in consecutive years, 2017 and 2018, and winner of three Emmy Awards.
illinois-state.evidence: Laurie Metcalf(1976) – one of the six actors to win Tony Awards in consecutive years (2017–2018); won three Emmy Awards...
illinois-state.line: Laurie Metcalf, class of 1976, is one of only six actors to win Tony Awards in back-to-back years, 2017 and 2018. Add three Emmys. The judges love a clean repeat.

illinois-state.name: John Malkovich
illinois-state.fact: Attended Illinois State and was awarded a degree in 2005.
illinois-state.evidence: John Malkovich, attended, and awarded a degree in 2005 – film and theater actor (In the Line of Fire, Rounders, Being J...
illinois-state.line: John Malkovich attended Illinois State, went off to make movies like In the Line of Fire, and was awarded his degree in 2005. Longest free skate to a diploma I have ever seen.

indiana-state.name: Willa Brown
indiana-state.fact: Graduated in 1927; earned a private pilot's license in 1938 and a commercial license in 1939, the first African American woman in the United States to earn either.
indiana-state.evidence: She attended Indiana State Teachers College where she graduated in 1927 with a bachelor's degree. | Brown earned a private pilot's license in 1938 and a commercial pilot's license in 1939, … | …becoming the first African American woman to earn either type of license in the United States. | She trained hundreds of pilots, several of whom went on to become Tuskegee Airmen; … | Willa Beatrice Brown (January 22, 1906 – July 18, 1992)
indiana-state.line: Willa Brown graduated here in 1927. By 1939 she held private and commercial pilot's licenses, the first African American woman in the country to earn either. Then she trained hundreds of pilots, some of them future Tuskegee Airmen.

indiana-state.name: Margaret Hill McCarter
indiana-state.known_for: first woman to address Republican convention
indiana-state.fact: An 1884 graduate, schoolteacher and writer who was the first woman to address a Republican National Convention.
indiana-state.evidence: Margaret Hill McCarter, 1884 A.B., schoolteacher, writer, and first woman to address a Republican National Convention
indiana-state.line: Margaret Hill McCarter, class of 1884, was a schoolteacher and a writer, and the first woman ever to address a Republican National Convention. A Sycamore had the microphone first, folks.

indiana-state.name: Jamal Khashoggi
indiana-state.known_for: Saudi dissident and Washington Post columnist
indiana-state.fact: Earned a B.S. in business administration in 1983 and became a Saudi dissident, author, editor and Washington Post columnist.
indiana-state.evidence: Jamal Khashoggi, B.S. business administration 1983; Saudi dissident, author, activist, editor, Washington Post columnist
indiana-state.line: Jamal Khashoggi earned his business degree in Terre Haute in 1983, then became an author, an editor, a Saudi dissident, and a Washington Post columnist. We say his name with respect.

indiana-state.name: Bubba the Love Sponge Clem
indiana-state.years: attended; dropped out in his second year
indiana-state.fact: Born Todd Alan Clem, he legally changed his name in October 1998; in January 2004 the FCC issued a $755,000 fine to Clear Channel and he was fired on February 23.
indiana-state.evidence: He attended Indiana State University in Terre Haute, Indiana, ... and he dropped out in his second year. | In October 1998, Clem legally changed his name to Bubba the Love Sponge Clem. | In January 2004, the FCC issued a $755,000 fine to Clear Channel Communications... | Clem was fired on February 23.
indiana-state.line: He dropped out of Indiana State in year two and legally became Bubba the Love Sponge Clem. In January 2004 the F C C fined Clear Channel seven hundred fifty-five thousand dollars, and he was fired that February. We will claim the first three semesters.

indiana-state.name: Birch Bayh
indiana-state.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
indiana-state.fact: U.S. senator from Indiana from 1963 to 1981 who authored two Constitutional amendments.
indiana-state.evidence: Birch Bayh, US senator, Indiana (1963–1981); authored two Constitutional amendments
indiana-state.line: Birch Bayh, a Sycamore, sat in the United States Senate for Indiana from 1963 to 1981 and authored two Constitutional amendments. Most of us never get one encore. He got two.

iona.name: John Sweeney
iona.fact: Sweeney graduated from Iona in 1956 with an economics degree, was elected president of the SEIU in 1980 and led the AFL-CIO from 1995 to 2009.
iona.evidence: "Sweeney enrolled at Iona College in New Rochelle in 1952." ... "In 1956, he graduated with a degree in economics." ... "In 1980, Sweeney was elected president of the national SEIU." ... "John Joseph Sweeney (May 5, 1934 – February 1, 2021) was an American labor leader who served as president of the AFL–CIO from 1995 to 2009."
iona.line: John Sweeney, Iona economics, class of fifty-six. Elected president of the S E I U in nineteen eighty, then ran the whole AFL-CIO from ninety-five to two thousand nine. A Gael who stood up for working people. That's my guy!

iona.name: Eileen Ivers
iona.years: Iona alumna (class year not given on the page)
iona.fact: Ivers, an Irish-American fiddle player, is listed among Iona's notable alumni.
iona.line: Eileen Ivers, Irish-American fiddle player, is one of ours. A Gael on the fiddle, come on, it doesn't get more New Rochelle than that!

iona.name: Don McLean
iona.fact: McLean attended night school at Iona and received a bachelor's degree in business administration in 1968; American Pie reached number one in January 1972.
iona.evidence: "McLean attended night school at Iona College and received a bachelor's degree in business administration in 1968." ... "He turned down a scholarship to Columbia University Graduate School" ... "reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 from January 15 to February 5, 1972"
iona.line: Don McLean went to night school at Iona, got his business degree in sixty-eight, and turned down a scholarship to Columbia. Four years later American Pie was number one. Good call, Donnie!

iona.name: Catherine R. Kinney
iona.years: Iona alumna (class year not given on the page)
iona.fact: Kinney, a former president of the New York Stock Exchange, is listed among Iona's notable alumni.
iona.evidence: "Catherine R. Kinney, former president of the New York Stock Exchange"
iona.line: Catherine Kinney, a Gael, became president of the New York Stock Exchange. From New Rochelle to Wall Street, that's a short train ride and a long climb.

iona.name: Alfred F. Kelly Jr.
iona.years: Iona alumnus (class year not given on the page)
iona.fact: Kelly, listed among Iona's notable alumni, served as chairman and CEO of Visa Inc.
iona.evidence: "Alfred F. Kelly Jr., chairman and CEO of Visa Inc."
iona.line: Al Kelly Junior, an Iona man, became chairman and CEO of Visa. So the next time you look at your credit card bill, Gaels, just know a little piece of that is school spirit.

iu-indy.name: Norman Bridwell
iu-indy.known_for: created Clifford the Big Red Dog
iu-indy.fact: Norman Bridwell, Herron class of 1950, was the author and illustrator of Clifford the Big Red Dog.
iu-indy.evidence: Norman Bridwell (Herron 1950), author and illustrator of Clifford the Big Red Dog
iu-indy.line: Norman Bridwell studied at Herron, class of 1950, and went on to write and draw Clifford the Big Red Dog. The biggest dog in children's books has Indy roots, and I will not be quiet about it.

iu-indy.name: Vija Celmins
iu-indy.fact: Vija Celmins, Herron class of 1961, is a fine art painter and printmaker.
iu-indy.evidence: Vija Celmins (Herron 1961), fine art painter and printmaker
iu-indy.line: Vija Celmins came out of Herron in 1961 and became a fine art painter and printmaker. Art school in Indianapolis, folks. It works.

iu-indy.name: David Wolf
iu-indy.fact: David Wolf, an astronaut, is listed among the school's notable alumni.
iu-indy.line: David Wolf is an astronaut and he's one of ours. Jaguars are fast, but that is a whole other kind of fast.

iu-indy.name: Dan Quayle
iu-indy.fact: Dan Quayle, law class of 1974, was the 44th Vice President of the United States.
iu-indy.evidence: Dan Quayle (Law 1974), 44th Vice President of the United States, former member of the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate
iu-indy.line: Dan Quayle got his law degree here in 1974 and ended up the forty-fourth Vice President. House, Senate, then number two in the country. Night school energy, honestly.

iu-indy.name: Dan Coats
iu-indy.known_for: senator turned lobbyist turned intelligence chief
iu-indy.fact: Dan Coats received his law degree in Indianapolis in 1971, and in 2007 co-chaired a team of lobbyists for Cooper Industries, a company that had moved its principal place of business to Bermuda.
iu-indy.evidence: Coats received a Juris Doctor from Indiana University Robert H. McKinney School of Law in 1971. ... and then worked as a lobbyist in Washington, D.C. ... In 2007, Coats served as co-chairman of a team of lobbyists for Cooper Industries, a Texas corporation that moved its principal place of business to Bermuda, where it would not be liable for U.S. taxes. In that role, he worked to block Senate legislation that would have closed a tax loophole, worth hundreds of millions of dollars to Cooper Industries. ... Daniel Ray Coats (born May 16, 1943) is an American politician, attorney, and diplomat
iu-indy.line: Dan Coats, law class of 1971. Later a lobbyist, in 2007 he worked to block a bill closing a tax loophole worth hundreds of millions to a company that had moved to Bermuda. We taught him the law. The loophole, he freelanced.

jacksonville.name: Alvin Brown
jacksonville.fact: Brown, who holds a BA and an MBA from Jacksonville University, won the 2011 mayoral race by 1,648 votes and became the first African American elected mayor of Jacksonville.
jacksonville.evidence: "Jacksonville University (BA, MBA)" ... "Brown became the first African American ever elected Mayor of Jacksonville" ... "On May 17, Brown narrowly defeated Hogan by 1,648 votes" ... "Brown was sworn in as mayor on July 1, 2011."
jacksonville.line: Mister Mayor! Alvin Brown, two JU degrees, won by one thousand six hundred forty-eight votes and became the first African American ever elected mayor of Jacksonville, sworn in back in twenty eleven. That is a Dolphin running the whole river.

jacksonville.name: William Forsythe
jacksonville.fact: Forsythe is listed in the university's notable alumni table as a dancer and choreographer.
jacksonville.evidence: Notable alumni table: "William Forsythe" – "Dancer and choreographer"
jacksonville.line: Not every Dolphin move happens on hardwood. William Forsythe, JU alum, made his name as a dancer and choreographer. Call him Billy Footwork. Best first step this school ever produced.

jacksonville.name: Bertice Berry
jacksonville.fact: Berry is listed in the university's notable alumni table as a sociologist.
jacksonville.line: Shout out to Doctor B. Bertice Berry, JU alum and sociologist. She studies how people behave in groups, so yes, she could explain our student section better than I can.

jacksonville.name: Jack Williams
jacksonville.fact: Williams is a journalist and the founding editor of the USA Today weather page.
jacksonville.evidence: Notable alumni table: "Jack Williams" – "Journalist and founding editor of the USA Today weather page"
jacksonville.line: You know that big colorful weather page in USA Today? A Dolphin started it. Jack Williams, JU alum, journalist, founding editor of that page. Weatherman Jack. Forecast in Duval is always green.

kent-state.name: Sarah Deal
kent-state.fact: Deal earned a B.S. in aerospace flight technology from Kent State in 1992 and became the Marine Corps' first female aviator in 1995.
kent-state.evidence: Deal earned a Bachelor of Science degree in aerospace flight technology from Kent State University in 1992. | subsequently became the Marine Corps' first female aviator in 1995. | and earned her aviator's wings on April 21, 1995. | Deal was assigned to Marine Heavy Helicopter Squadron 466 as a CH-53E pilot.
kent-state.line: Sarah Deal, flight technology degree, class of 1992. Three years later she earned her wings and became the Marine Corps' first female aviator, flying heavy helicopters. First. Ever. That's a Golden Flash.

kent-state.name: Arnulfo Trejo
kent-state.fact: Trejo earned an M.A. in library science from Kent State in 1953 and in 1971 co-founded the National Association of Spanish Speaking Librarians, known as REFORMA.
kent-state.evidence: M.A. in Library Science, Kent State University, 1953 | In 1971 he and Elizabeth Martinez founded the National Association of Spanish Speaking Librarians | In 1975 he founded the Graduate Library Institute for Spanish-speaking Americans | Arnulfo Duenes Trejo (August 15, 1922 – July 5, 2002) || List page: Arnulfo Trejo: Founder of REFORMA, an organization to promote library services to Latinos and Spanish-speaking individuals in the US | M.A. Library Science (1953)
kent-state.line: Arnulfo Trejo got his library science master's here in 1953. In 1971 he co-founded REFORMA to promote library services for Latinos and Spanish speakers. Guy saw who the library was leaving out and fixed it.

kent-state.name: Connie Schultz
kent-state.fact: Connie Schultz, journalism 1979, was a columnist for The Plain Dealer and a 2005 Pulitzer Prize winner.
kent-state.evidence: Connie Schultz: Columnist for The Plain Dealer, 2005 Pulitzer Prize winner | Journalism (1979)
kent-state.line: Connie Schultz, journalism, 1979. Columnist for The Plain Dealer, Pulitzer Prize winner in 2005. Northeast Ohio, a newspaper column, and a Pulitzer. You can't draw it up better.

kent-state.name: Kyle Craven
kent-state.fact: Kyle Craven, the internet celebrity from the Bad Luck Brian meme, earned a B.S. in construction management from Kent State in 2012.
kent-state.evidence: Kyle Craven: Internet celebrity from the Bad Luck Brian meme | B.S. Construction Management (2012)
kent-state.line: You know the Bad Luck Brian meme? That's Kyle Craven, Kent State construction management, class of 2012. Bad luck on the internet, good luck on the diploma.

kent-state.name: Carl E. Walz
kent-state.fact: Astronaut Carl E. Walz earned a B.S. in physics from Kent State in 1977.
kent-state.evidence: Carl E. Walz: Astronaut | B.S. Physics (1977)
kent-state.line: Carl Walz, physics degree, 1977, became an astronaut. So when I say this program is going places, understand that one of us already left the planet.

la-salle.name: Charles Fuller
la-salle.fact: Fuller studied at La Salle from 1965 to 1967 and received the 1982 Pulitzer Prize for Drama for A Soldier's Play.
la-salle.evidence: "he attended Roman Catholic High School and then Villanova University (1956–1958)" "later studied at La Salle University (1965–1967), earning a DFA" "for which he received the 1982 Pulitzer Prize for Drama" "being produced as the 1984 film A Soldier's Story" "Charles H. Fuller Jr. (March 5, 1939 – October 3, 2022)"
la-salle.line: Darlings, Charles Fuller studied at La Salle from nineteen sixty-five to sixty-seven, then won the nineteen eighty-two Pulitzer Prize for Drama for A Soldier's Play. Bravo, bravo, and a curtain call!

lipscomb.name: J. Ridley Stroop
lipscomb.fact: Stroop earned his Lipscomb diploma in 1921, published his interference study in 1935, and taught psychology and Biblical studies until retiring in 1967.
lipscomb.evidence: "Two years later, in 1921, he obtained his diploma from Lipscomb" ... "He soon returned to David Lipscomb College, where he served as Registrar for eleven years." ... "Stroop continued to teach psychology and Biblical studies until he retired in 1967." Lipscomb University page: "J. Ridley Stroop(1921), psychology and biblical professor, known for his interference research in..."
lipscomb.line: J. Ridley Stroop got his Lipscomb diploma in nineteen twenty-one and became known for his interference research. Then he came home, served eleven years as registrar, and taught psychology and Bible until nineteen sixty-seven. A scientist who stayed put. Imagine.

lipscomb.name: Jim Jinkins
lipscomb.fact: Jinkins, Lipscomb class of 1975, established Jumbo Pictures in 1990 to produce Doug for Nickelodeon and sold the company to Disney in 1996.
lipscomb.evidence: "Education: Lipscomb University" ... "Jinkins established Jumbo Pictures in 1990 to produce Doug for Nickelodeon." ... "In 1996, Jinkins sold Jumbo Pictures to Disney." ... "Jinkins had developed Doug Funnie through doodles during the early days of his career." Lipscomb University page: "Jim Jinkins(1975), creator of the animated Doug series"
lipscomb.line: Jim Jinkins, class of seventy-five, turned his doodles into Doug Funnie. He started Jumbo Pictures in nineteen ninety to make Doug for Nickelodeon, then sold it to Disney six years later. Not bad for a doodler, bless him.

lipscomb.name: Edwin Trevathan
lipscomb.fact: Trevathan, Lipscomb class of 1977, is a physician and public health leader.
lipscomb.evidence: "Edwin Trevathan(1977), physician and public health leader, currently director of the Vanderbilt Institute..."
lipscomb.line: Edwin Trevathan, class of seventy-seven, became a physician and a public health leader, and he directs an institute over at Vanderbilt. We will forgive him the address. The work is what counts.

lipscomb.name: Michael Shane Neal
lipscomb.fact: Neal, Lipscomb class of 1991, is a portrait artist.
lipscomb.line: Michael Shane Neal, class of ninety-one, paints portraits for a living. So if any Bison wants to be remembered kindly, I would suggest good manners and a good rebound margin.

lipscomb.name: W. Mark Lanier
lipscomb.known_for: trial lawyer, founded Lanier Law Firm
lipscomb.fact: Lanier, Lipscomb class of 1981, is the founder of The Lanier Law Firm.
lipscomb.evidence: "W. Mark Lanier(1981), founder of The Lanier Law Firm"
lipscomb.line: W. Mark Lanier, class of eighty-one, founded The Lanier Law Firm and put his own name right on the door. That is confidence, y'all. I do admire it.

long-beach-state.name: Erin Gruwell
long-beach-state.years: master's degree and teaching credentials; year not listed on source
long-beach-state.fact: Erin Gruwell earned her master's degree and teaching credentials at Cal State Long Beach and began student teaching in 1994 at Woodrow Wilson High School in Long Beach; all 150 of her Freedom Writers graduated from high school.
long-beach-state.evidence: She earned her master's degree and teaching credentials from California State University, Long Beach,… | Gruwell began student teaching in 1994 at Woodrow Wilson High School in Long Beach, California. | All 150 Freedom Writers graduated from high school and many went on to attend college. | It is the basis of the 2007 movie Freedom Writers, starring Hilary Swank as Gruwell,
long-beach-state.line: Erin Gruwell earned her teaching credentials at Long Beach State and started at Wilson High in nineteen ninety four. All one hundred fifty of her Freedom Writers graduated. Hilary Swank played her in the movie, but the real work happened here.

long-beach-state.name: Linda Woolverton
long-beach-state.fact: Linda Woolverton, born in Long Beach in 1952, graduated from Cal State Long Beach with a BFA in theater arts in 1973 and became the first female screenwriter with a sole writing credit on a film that grossed $1 billion.
long-beach-state.evidence: Woolverton was born in 1952 in Long Beach, California. | She attended California State University, Long Beach, graduating with a BFA in theater arts in 1973. | making Woolverton the first female screenwriter with a sole writing credit on a film that grossed $1 billion
long-beach-state.line: Linda Woolverton was born in Long Beach and finished her theater degree at the Beach in seventy three. She became the first woman with a sole writing credit on a film that grossed a billion dollars. Hometown girl, worldwide audience.

long-beach-state.name: Steven Spielberg
long-beach-state.fact: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg was a student at Cal State Long Beach from 1965 to 1969 and again from 2001 to 2002.
long-beach-state.line: Steven Spielberg was a student here from nineteen sixty five to sixty nine, and then again in two thousand one. Three decades between semesters. At the Beach, we hold your seat.

long-beach-state.name: Palmer Luckey
long-beach-state.fact: Palmer Luckey, born 1992, majored in journalism at CSU Long Beach before dropping out, co-founded the defense technology company Anduril Industries, and as of September 2026 Forbes values his net worth at $6 billion.
long-beach-state.evidence: California State University, Long Beach (attended) | He later majored in journalism at CSU Long Beach... | Luckey dropped out of university to focus on it full-time. | American entrepreneur and co-founder of defense technology company Anduril Industries. | a military technology company focused on autonomous drones and sensors for military applications. | As of September 2026, Forbes values his net worth at $6 billion.
long-beach-state.line: Palmer Luckey majored in journalism here, dropped out, and co-founded a military technology company built on autonomous drones. Forbes puts him at six billion dollars. The journalism degree, I gather, remains unfinished.

long-beach-state.name: Chris Carter
long-beach-state.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
long-beach-state.fact: Chris Carter, on Cal State Long Beach's alumni list, is the creator and producer of the X-Files.
long-beach-state.evidence: Chris Carter: creator and producer of the X-Files
long-beach-state.line: Chris Carter, creator and producer of the X-Files, is a Long Beach State alum. The truth is out there, and apparently it started on our campus.

loyola-chicago.name: Mamie Till-Mobley
loyola-chicago.fact: Till-Mobley earned a master's degree in educational administration from Loyola University Chicago in 1971 and taught for 23 years in the Chicago public schools.
loyola-chicago.evidence: "In 1971, Till-Mobley earned a master's degree in educational administration from Loyola University Chicago." "For her son's funeral, Mamie Till insisted that the casket containing his body be left open." "Tens of thousands of people viewed Emmett's body, and photographs circulated around the country." "including 23 years teaching in the Chicago public school system." "(born Mamie Elizabeth Carthan; November 23, 1921 – January 6, 2003)"
loyola-chicago.line: Mamie Till-Mobley insisted her son Emmett's casket be left open, and tens of thousands saw. She taught twenty-three years in Chicago's public schools and earned a Loyola master's degree in nineteen seventy-one. Blessed be her memory.

loyola-chicago.name: Maria Pappas
loyola-chicago.fact: Pappas earned her Ph.D. in psychology from Loyola in 1976 and has been Cook County Treasurer since 1998.
loyola-chicago.evidence: "Maria Pappas, Cook County Treasurer (1998–present); earned her Ph.D. in psychology from Loyola in 1976"
loyola-chicago.line: Maria Pappas earned her doctorate in psychology from Loyola in nineteen seventy-six, and has served as Cook County Treasurer since nineteen ninety-eight. Faithful stewardship, my friends.

loyola-chicago.name: Michael Madigan
loyola-chicago.fact: Madigan graduated from Loyola's law school in 1967, was Illinois House Speaker from 1983 to 2021 except 1995-97, and was convicted on ten counts on February 12, 2025.
loyola-chicago.evidence: "Madigan graduated from Loyola Law School in 1967." "University of Notre Dame (BA) Loyola University Chicago (JD)" "Madigan was Speaker of the Illinois House from 1983 to 2021, with the exception of 1995–97," "On February 12, 2025, Madigan was convicted on ten counts of bribery, wire fraud, and Travel Act violations." "He was sentenced to 7½ years in prison and a $2.5 million fine."
loyola-chicago.line: We pray also for Michael Madigan, Loyola Law, nineteen sixty-seven. Speaker of the Illinois House for most of four decades, convicted in twenty twenty-five on ten counts including bribery, and sentenced to seven and a half years. Confession is good for the soul.

loyola-chicago.name: Richard Kiley
loyola-chicago.fact: Kiley, an Emmy-winning actor, singer and narrator, attended Loyola.
loyola-chicago.evidence: "Richard Kiley, Emmy-winning actor, singer and narrator(attended)"
loyola-chicago.line: Richard Kiley, the Emmy-winning actor, singer and narrator, attended Loyola. A voice like that, one suspects, was a gift from above.

manhattan.name: Michael Walsh
manhattan.fact: Walsh graduated from Manhattan with a B.S. in 1966, directed motor vehicle pollution control at the EPA from 1974 to 1981 and received a MacArthur genius grant in 2005.
manhattan.evidence: "Walsh graduated from Manhattan College with a B.S. (1966)" ... "He worked in government service, directing motor vehicle pollution control efforts in the City of New York Department of Air Resources (1970–74) and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (1974–81)." ... "In 2005, he received a "genius grant" from the MacArthur Fellows Program."
manhattan.line: Michael Walsh, class of sixty-six, ran motor vehicle pollution control for New York City and then for the EPA. In two thousand five he got a MacArthur genius grant. Cleaner air, courtesy of a Jasper. You're welcome.

manhattan.name: James W. Cooley
manhattan.years: Manhattan graduate (class year not given on the page)
manhattan.known_for: co-author of the fast Fourier transform
manhattan.fact: Cooley, a mathematician, co-authored the FFT (fast Fourier transform) algorithm used in digital processing.
manhattan.evidence: "This is a list of notable graduates of Manhattan University in Riverdale, New York." ... "James W. Cooley – mathematician, co-author of the FFT (fast Fourier transform) algorithm used in digital processing"
manhattan.line: James Cooley, a Jasper mathematician, co-wrote the fast Fourier transform, the algorithm behind digital processing. So this very broadcast is running on Riverdale math. Listen up and say thank you.

manhattan.name: James Patterson
manhattan.years: Manhattan graduate (class year not given on the page)
manhattan.fact: Patterson is a New York Times best-selling and Edgar Award-winning novelist, author of Along Came a Spider and Kiss the Girls.
manhattan.evidence: "This is a list of notable graduates of Manhattan University in Riverdale, New York." ... "James Patterson – New York Times best-selling and Edgar Award-winning novelist, author of Along Came a Spider and Kiss the Girls"
manhattan.line: James Patterson, the best-selling novelist behind Along Came a Spider and Kiss the Girls, is a Jasper. Whatever airport you're in right now, there's a little piece of Riverdale by the register.

manhattan.name: Hugo Montenegro
manhattan.years: Manhattan graduate (class year not given on the page)
manhattan.fact: Montenegro was a TV and movie soundtrack composer whose credits include I Dream of Jeannie.
manhattan.evidence: "This is a list of notable graduates of Manhattan University in Riverdale, New York." ... "Hugo Montenegro – TV and movie soundtrack composer, I Dream of Jeannie and The Outcasts"
manhattan.line: Hugo Montenegro, a Jasper, composed soundtracks for TV and the movies, I Dream of Jeannie included. So that tune stuck in your head? Blame the Bronx.

manhattan.name: Rudy Giuliani
manhattan.fact: Giuliani graduated from Manhattan in 1965; he was disbarred in New York on July 2, 2024, and in the District of Columbia on September 26, 2024, after losing a $148-million defamation lawsuit in 2023.
manhattan.evidence: "Giuliani attended Manhattan College in Riverdale, Bronx, where he majored in political science with a minor in philosophy." ... "He graduated in 1965." ... "On July 2, 2024, he was disbarred in the state of New York." ... "On September 26, 2024, he was disbarred in the District of Columbia under reciprocal discipline." ... "Later in 2023, Giuliani lost a $148-million defamation lawsuit for his false claims about two election workers in Georgia,"
manhattan.line: Rudy Giuliani, class of sixty-five, political science. Lost a hundred and forty-eight million dollar defamation suit in twenty twenty-three, then got disbarred in New York and in Washington in twenty twenty-four. We claim him, Jaspers. We just don't retain him.

marist.name: Gina Trapani
marist.fact: Trapani, class of 1997, founded Lifehacker and was listed among Fast Company's Most Influential Women in Technology in 2009 and 2010.
marist.evidence: "Gina Trapani '97 – founder of Lifehacker; listed among Fast Company's Most Influential Women in Technology in 2009 and 2010"
marist.line: Gina Trapani, class of ninety-seven, founded Lifehacker and made Fast Company's list of the most influential women in technology two years running. That's good tape, Red Foxes.

marist.name: Ian O'Connor
marist.fact: O'Connor, class of 1986, is a New York Times best-selling author and national sports columnist.
marist.evidence: "Ian O'Connor '86 – New York Times best-selling author and national sports columnist"
marist.line: Ian O'Connor, class of eighty-six, is a New York Times best-selling author and a national sports columnist. A writer who meets deadlines. As a coach, I respect the fundamentals.

marist.name: Adam Ferrara
marist.fact: Ferrara, class of 1988, is an actor and comedian.
marist.line: Adam Ferrara, class of eighty-eight, is an actor and comedian. So Marist does produce funny people. I'm told I'm not one of them.

marist.name: Jeff Sutphen
marist.fact: Sutphen, class of 1998, hosted the game show BrainSurge on Nickelodeon.
marist.evidence: "Jeff Sutphen '98 – host of the game show BrainSurge on Nickelodeon"
marist.line: Jeff Sutphen, class of ninety-eight, hosted the Nickelodeon game show BrainSurge. A Red Fox running a game show for kids. Honestly, not that different from coaching.

marist.name: Bill O'Reilly
marist.fact: O'Reilly received a Bachelor of Arts in history from Marist in 1971; in 2017 he was dismissed from Fox News, which announced on April 19 that he would not be returning.
marist.evidence: "After graduating from Chaminade in 1967, O'Reilly attended Marist College in Poughkeepsie, New York." ... "He received his Bachelor of Arts degree in history in 1971." ... "In 2017, O'Reilly was dismissed from Fox News" ... "On April 19, Fox News announced that O'Reilly would not be returning to the network."
marist.line: Bill O'Reilly, history degree, class of seventy-one. In twenty seventeen Fox News dismissed him and announced he would not be returning. Red Foxes, we'll log it on the tape and keep the film moving.

merrimack.name: Kelly Lange
merrimack.years: Merrimack graduate (class year not given on the page)
merrimack.known_for: first woman nightly anchor in L.A.
merrimack.fact: Lange graduated from Merrimack, started at KNBC as a weather forecaster in March 1971, was promoted to news anchor in December 1976, and is noted as the first woman to be a nightly news anchor in Los Angeles.
merrimack.evidence: "and graduated from Merrimack College in North Andover, Massachusetts." ... "most notable for being the first woman to be a nightly news anchor in Los Angeles" ... "Lange started in March 1971 as a weather forecaster for KNBC's weeknight newscasts" ... "In December 1976 Lange was promoted to news anchor,"
merrimack.line: Kelly Lange graduated from Merrimack, started doing weather in Los Angeles in nineteen seventy-one, and five years later became the first woman to anchor a nightly newscast there. Wicked proud of that one, Warriors!

merrimack.name: Barbara L'Italien
merrimack.years: listed by Merrimack (class year not given on the page)
merrimack.fact: L'Italien served as a Massachusetts state representative and as a member of the state senate.
merrimack.evidence: [Merrimack_College article, notable-people list] "Barbara L'Italien- Massachusetts state representative and former member of the senate"
merrimack.line: Barbara L'Italien served Massachusetts as a state representative and in the state senate. Public service, right up the road. Love to see it, Warriors!

merrimack.name: Charlie Day
merrimack.years: listed by Merrimack (class year not given on the page)
merrimack.fact: Day, an actor and comedian, is listed among Merrimack's notable people.
merrimack.evidence: [Merrimack_College article, notable-people list] "Charlie Day- actor and comedian"
merrimack.line: Charlie Day, actor and comedian, is on Merrimack's list. A Warrior who makes people laugh for a living. Honestly, same!

merrimack.name: T. J. Donovan
merrimack.years: listed by Merrimack (class year not given on the page)
merrimack.fact: Donovan is a former attorney general of Vermont.
merrimack.evidence: [Merrimack_College article, notable-people list] "T. J. Donovan- former attorney general of Vermont"
merrimack.line: T. J. Donovan went from Merrimack's list to attorney general of Vermont. So yes, Warriors, we've got a top cop one state over.

miami-oh.name: Rita Dove
miami-oh.years: alumna per the list page; year not given

oakland.name: Karen Batchelor
oakland.years: B.A. in psychology (year not stated on source page)
oakland.known_for: first Black member of the DAR
oakland.fact: Karen Batchelor, an Oakland psychology graduate, became the first-known Black member of the Daughters of the American Revolution in October 1977.
oakland.evidence: She majored in anthropology at Fisk University before transferring to Oakland University, where she graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in psychology. ... In October 1977, during the administration of President General Jeannette Osborn Baylies, Batchelor became the first-known black member of the Daughters of the American Revolution when she joined the Ezra Parker chapter in Royal Oak, Michigan. ... In 1979, Batchelor co-founded the Fred Hart Williams Genealogical Society, which researches and preserves African-American family history.
oakland.line: Karen Batchelor got her psychology degree at Oakland, sugar, and in 1977 she became the first known Black member of the Daughters of the American Revolution. Two years later she co-founded a society to preserve African-American family history. She did the homework.

oakland.name: Regina Carter
oakland.fact: Regina Carter graduated from Oakland University in 1985 as a jazz major and was awarded a MacArthur fellowship in September 2006.
oakland.evidence: She transferred to Oakland University in Rochester, Michigan, where she was a jazz major under the direction of Marvin "Doc" Holladay. She graduated in 1985. ... Carter was awarded a MacArthur Fellows Program grant, also known as a "genius grant", in September 2006. ... In December 2001, she played a concert in Genoa using Il Cannone Guarnerius, a violin that was made in 1743 and was once owned and favoured by Niccolò Paganini.
oakland.line: Regina Carter was a jazz major here, class of 1985. In 2001 she played a concert in Genoa on Paganini's own violin, built in 1743, and in 2006 she won a MacArthur genius grant. Our girl.

oakland.name: Jayne Houdyshell

oakland.evidence: Jayne Houdyshell – Broadway actress, Tony Award winner
oakland.line: Jayne Houdyshell went from Oakland to Broadway and won herself a Tony Award. Rochester, Michigan to the bright lights, honey. Grizzlies travel well.

oakland.name: David Hasselhoff

oakland.line: David Hasselhoff attended Oakland. Attended, sugar, I did not say graduated. But he sat in our chairs, so we're keeping him.

oakland.evidence: Maximiliano Larroquette – designer of Chevrolet Volt
oakland.line: Maximiliano Larroquette, one of ours, designed the Chevrolet Volt. A Golden Grizzly drew up that car. You're welcome, Detroit.

ohio.name: Marie Tharp
ohio.fact: Tharp graduated from Ohio University in 1943 and in the 1950s co-produced the first scientific map of the Atlantic Ocean floor, discovering the rift valley of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
ohio.evidence: She entered the Ohio University in 1939, where she "changed her major every semester." | Tharp graduated from Ohio University in 1943 with bachelor's degrees in English and music and four minors. | In the 1950s, she collaborated with geologist Bruce Heezen to produce the first scientific map of the Atlantic Ocean floor. | Marie Tharp also discovered the rift valley on her more precise graphical representations of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. | It took her a year to convince Bruce Heezen of this. | Instead, for a time, he favored the Expanding Earth hypothesis, dismissing her explanation as "girl talk".
ohio.line: Marie Tharp changed her major every semester here and graduated in 1943. Then she helped draw the first scientific map of the Atlantic floor and found the rift valley in it. Her partner called it girl talk. Took her a year to convince him.

ohio.line: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, a structural biologist and an Ohio University alum, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009. Folks around here don't brag much, but we'll make an exception for a Nobel.

ohio.name: Yvette McGee Brown
ohio.years: alumna per the list page; year not given

ohio.evidence: Yvette McGee Brown, first African-American female justice of the Supreme Court of Ohio
ohio.line: Yvette McGee Brown became the first African-American woman to sit as a justice on the Supreme Court of Ohio. That road to Columbus ran right through Athens.

ohio.evidence: subsequently earned an MBA from Ohio University in the United States. | He confessed to an accounting fraud to the tune of ₹7,000 crore or $1.5 billion | resigned from the Satyam board on 7 January 2009. | In 2015, he was convicted of corporate fraud, which led to the collapse of Satyam Computers. | On 9 April 2015, Ramalinga Raju and his brothers were sentenced to 7 years in jail, fined ₹5.5 crore.
ohio.line: Ramalinga Raju earned his M B A here. He later confessed to a one and a half billion dollar accounting fraud at Satyam Computers, and in 2015 he was convicted and sentenced to seven years. We taught him business. Evidently not that kind.

ohio.name: Jerri Nielsen
ohio.years: alumna per the list page; year not given

ohio.line: Jerri Nielsen was a physician in Antarctica. Antarctica. Next time you complain about an Athens winter, think about her commute.

purdue-fort-wayne.line: Julia Barr, actress, All My Children. She's on the Fort Wayne list too. Daytime drama, Mastodon roots.

"a National Book Award for Young People's Literature for The Night Swimmers (1980)." ... queens.line: Betsy Byars, English degree, class of nineteen fifty. One Newbery Medal in nineteen seventy-one, one National Book Award in nineteen eighty, and one pilot's license. She lived on an airstrip. That is a strong balance sheet.

queens.line: Becky Douglas attended Queens on a full violin scholarship. In two thousand one she founded Rising Star Outreach and became a philanthropist. A full ride, repaid to the world with interest. I approve of that return.

queens.name: Elizabeth Johnston Evans Johnston

queens.evidence: "Elizabeth Johnston Evans Johnston(1851–1934), philanthropist and social worker"
queens.line: From the older ledgers: Elizabeth Johnston Evans Johnston, born eighteen fifty-one, philanthropist and social worker. She gave her time and her money away. Not how bankers usually keep score, but the Royals count it.

quinnipiac.name: William D. Euille
quinnipiac.known_for: first Black mayor of Alexandria, Virginia
quinnipiac.fact: Euille earned an accounting degree from Quinnipiac in 1972 and served from 2003 to 2016 as the first African-American mayor of Alexandria, Virginia.
quinnipiac.evidence: "and earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from Quinnipiac University in Hamden, Connecticut in 1972." ... "from 2003 until 2016, serving as the first African-American in the city's history to hold that position." ... "He was elected the city's first African-American mayor in May 2003"
quinnipiac.line: William Euille, accounting degree, class of seventy-two. In two thousand three he was elected the first African-American mayor of Alexandria, Virginia, and he held the job until twenty sixteen. Thirteen years. The numbers speak, Bobcats.

"In November 1961, he founded the Syracuse chapter of Congress of Racial Equality." "He was a founder of the National Welfare Rights Organization." "George Alvin Wiley (February 26, 1931 – August 8, 1973) was an American"
rhode-island.line: George Wiley, class of fifty-three! A chemist with a Cornell doctorate who founded the Syracuse chapter of the Congress of Racial Equality in sixty-one, and was a founder of the National Welfare Rights Organization. A fine captain, that one!

rhode-island.name: William B. Gould IV

rhode-island.line: William Gould the Fourth, class of fifty-eight, chaired the National Labor Relations Board from ninety-four to ninety-eight. A steady hand on the tiller!

rhode-island.name: Robert Crandall
rhode-island.fact: Crandall graduated from URI and, as head of American Airlines, told Braniff's CEO in 1982 that if Braniff raised its prices, American would too.
rhode-island.evidence: "He graduated from the University of Rhode Island, and from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, with an MBA." "Robert Crandall (1960) – former president and chairman of the board, American Airlines" (list page) "In 1982, he had a famous conversation with Braniff CEO Howard D. Putnam, in which he told Putnam that if Braniff raised their prices, American would too." "Crandall has publicly expressed embarrassment over that conversation." "Born: December 6, 1935 (age 90) Westerly, Rhode Island, U.S."
rhode-island.line: Then there's Bob Crandall, class of nineteen sixty, boss of American Airlines. In eighty-two he told the head of Braniff that if Braniff raised prices, American would too. Says he's embarrassed about it. Aye, I'd wager so!

rhode-island.name: Christiane Amanpour
rhode-island.fact: Amanpour, B.A. 1983, is a journalist and CNN correspondent.
rhode-island.line: Christiane Amanpour, class of eighty-three, journalist and CNN correspondent. A Ram the whole world tunes in to!

rhode-island.name: Masta Ace

rhode-island.line: And Masta Ace, the rapper, class of eighty-eight. Proof a Ram can drop a rhyme as well as an anchor!

"Melvin was chosen by the Detroit Lions in the 11th round of the 1986 NFL draft as a wide receiver." "Melvin flew two missions on the Space Shuttle Atlantis as a mission specialist on STS-122 and STS-129." "In all, Melvin logged over 565 hours in space." "Leland Devon Melvin (born February 15, 1964)"
richmond.line: Five, six, seven, eight! Leland Melvin came to Richmond on a football scholarship, earned a chemistry degree, got drafted by the Detroit Lions in eighty-six, then flew two shuttle missions and logged over five hundred sixty-five hours in space!

richmond.name: Brett Wigdortz

richmond.evidence: "Frank E. Resnik( MS, 1955) – Philip Morris USA chairman and CEO"
richmond.line: And a one, and a two. Frank Resnik, master's degree, nineteen fifty-five, went on to be chairman and CEO of Philip Morris USA. Yes, that Philip Morris. We'll just keep marching.

richmond.name: E. Claiborne Robins Sr.
richmond.years: undergraduate studies (year not given on page)

"Robins died on July 6, 1995 at the age of 84."
richmond.line: E. Claiborne Robins did his undergraduate studies at Richmond, and in nineteen sixty-nine gave the school fifty million dollars in company stock plus ten million in cash, then the largest gift ever made to an American university. Now that's a halftime show!

Doe of Liberia, Nicolae Ceauşescu of Romania, Mobutu Sésé Seko of the then- Zaire and the Burmese embassy in the United States." ... "Von Kloberg himself reveled in the motto, "Shame is for sissies."" ... "lobbyist, infamous for his representation of some of the most notorious dictators of the 20th century."
rider.line: Edward von Kloberg the third, class of sixty-five, was a Washington lobbyist. His clients: Saddam Hussein, Ceausescu, Mobutu. His motto was shame is for sissies. Here's the scoop, Broncs, we're listing him. We're not framing him.

She also served twice as the Director for Africa at the National Security Council at the White House
robert-morris.line: Robin Sanders was the American ambassador to the Republic of the Congo, then to Nigeria, and twice ran Africa policy at the National Security Council. Then in 2010 she finished a doctorate at Robert Morris. Some people just don't sit still.

robert-morris.evidence: Max Baer, Pennsylvania Supreme Court Justice (2003-2022)
robert-morris.line: Max Baer was elected to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court in 2003 and served until 2022, rising to chief justice. Nearly two decades on the highest bench in the state, and he's on our list.

sacramento-state.name: Ryan Coogler

sacramento-state.line: Ryan Coogler left Sac State in two thousand seven with a finance degree. He became the first African American director at Marvel Studios, and his film Sinners set the Oscar record with sixteen nominations. He took home Best Original Screenplay. Hornet.

"served as the 4th Senior Enlisted Advisor to the Chairman (SEAC) from December 13, 2019 to November 3, 2023."
sacred-heart.line: Ramón Colón-López did two semesters at Sacred Heart, then enlisted in the Air Force. He became the first Hispanic airman to get the Combat Action Medal and rose to senior enlisted advisor to the chairman of the Joint Chiefs. Let's go!
