sacred-heart.fact: Ratzenberger attended Sacred Heart, worked the 1969 Woodstock Festival as a heavy equipment operator, played Cliff Clavin on Cheers and has voiced characters in 24 Pixar films.
sacred-heart.evidence: "Ratzenberger attended St. Ann's School, Fairfield Prep, and Bassick High School in Bridgeport and then Sacred Heart University in Fairfield, Connecticut." ... "In 1969, Ratzenberger worked at the Woodstock Festival as a heavy equipment operator" ... "Ratzenberger played mail carrier Cliff Clavin on the sitcom Cheers." ... "Ratzenberger has voiced characters in 24 Pixar films."
sacred-heart.line: John Ratzenberger went to Sacred Heart, ran heavy equipment at Woodstock in sixty-nine, played Cliff the mailman on Cheers, and has voiced characters in twenty-four Pixar films. Twenty-four! That's a stat line, Pioneers!

sacred-heart.name: Kevin Nealon
sacred-heart.years: Sacred Heart alumnus (class year not given on the page)
sacred-heart.fact: Nealon is an actor and was a Saturday Night Live cast member.
sacred-heart.evidence: [Sacred_Heart_University article, alumni list] "Kevin Nealon- actor, Saturday Night Live cast member"
sacred-heart.line: Kevin Nealon, actor and Saturday Night Live cast member, is a Pioneer. Live from Fairfield, baby!

sacred-heart.name: Lydia Hearst-Shaw
sacred-heart.years: Sacred Heart alumna (class year not given on the page)
sacred-heart.fact: Hearst-Shaw is a model and actress.
sacred-heart.evidence: [Sacred_Heart_University article, alumni list] "Lydia Hearst-Shaw- model and actress"
sacred-heart.line: Lydia Hearst-Shaw, model and actress, is on the Sacred Heart alumni list. Runway to red carpet, Pioneers get around.

saint-josephs.name: Sister Mary Scullion
saint-josephs.fact: Scullion earned a bachelor's degree in psychology from Saint Joseph's in 1976 and co-founded Project H.O.M.E. in 1989.
saint-josephs.evidence: "Scullion attended Temple University for one year before transferring to St. Joseph's University" "where she earned a Bachelor's degree in psychology in 1976." "In 1989, the two women co-founded Project H.O.M.E." "Her advocacy efforts have helped to establish the right of homeless persons to vote." "Sister Mary Scullion– co-founder and executive director, Project H.O.M.E." (list page)
saint-josephs.line: Sister Mary Scullion, class of seventy-six, co-founded Project HOME in nineteen eighty-nine and helped establish the right of homeless persons to vote. Now that, beautiful people, is a headliner.

saint-josephs.name: Kathleen McGinty
saint-josephs.fact: McGinty graduated from Saint Joseph's in 1985 with a BS in chemistry and chaired the White House Council on Environmental Quality from 1995 to 1998.
saint-josephs.evidence: "She graduated from St. Hubert Catholic High School for Girls, Saint Joseph's University in 1985 (with a BS in chemistry), and Columbia Law School in 1988 (with a JD)." "She chaired the White House Council on Environmental Quality from 1995 to 1998." "In 2003 she was appointed as the secretary of Pennsylvania's Department of Environmental Protection, serving in Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell's administration for over five years." "Kathleen Alana McGinty (born May 11, 1963)"
saint-josephs.line: Kathleen McGinty, chemistry degree, class of eighty-five, chaired the White House Council on Environmental Quality from ninety-five to ninety-eight, then ran Pennsylvania's Department of Environmental Protection. Smooth, baby. Real smooth.

saint-josephs.name: Chris Gheysens
saint-josephs.fact: Gheysens, MBA 2005, is president and chief executive officer of Wawa Inc.
saint-josephs.evidence: "Chris Gheysens(MBA 2005) – president and chief executive officer of Wawa Inc."
saint-josephs.line: And Chris Gheysens, MBA, two thousand five, is president and chief executive of Wawa. So every Wawa run, in a way, is a Hawk production. You're welcome.

saint-louis.name: Freeman Bosley Jr.
saint-louis.known_for: first Black mayor of St. Louis
saint-louis.fact: Bosley, B.A. 1976 and J.D. 1979, was St. Louis's first African-American mayor.
saint-louis.evidence: "Freeman Bosley Jr.(B.A. 1976; J.D. 1979) – St. Louis, Missouri's first African-American mayor"
saint-louis.line: Freeman Bosley Junior, bachelor's in seventy-six, law degree in seventy-nine, became the first African-American mayor of Saint Louis. All hail!

saint-louis.name: Irene D. Long
saint-louis.known_for: Kennedy Space Center chief medical officer
saint-louis.fact: Long, M.D. 1977, was the first female chief medical officer at Kennedy Space Center.
saint-louis.evidence: "Irene D. Long(M.D. 1977) – First female chief medical officer at Kennedy Space Center."
saint-louis.line: Irene Long, doctor of medicine, nineteen seventy-seven, the first female chief medical officer at Kennedy Space Center. What a piece of work is a Billiken!

saint-louis.name: Gene Kranz
saint-louis.fact: Kranz, B.S. 1954, was lead NASA flight director during the Apollo 11 Moon landing.
saint-louis.evidence: "Gene Kranz(B.S. 1954) – Lead NASA flight director during the Apollo 11 Moon landing"
saint-louis.line: Gene Kranz, class of nineteen fifty-four, was lead NASA flight director during the Apollo Eleven Moon landing. All the world's a stage, and he ran mission control.

saint-louis.name: Walden O'Dell
saint-louis.years: B.S. and M.S. in electrical engineering (years not given on page)
saint-louis.fact: O'Dell, who holds two electrical engineering degrees from Saint Louis University, wrote in an August 13, 2003 letter that he was committed to helping Ohio deliver its electoral votes to the President, and left Diebold in December 2005.
saint-louis.evidence: "O'Dell holds both a bachelor's and a master's degree in electrical engineering from Saint Louis University." "Walden O'Dell(B.S.; M.S.) – CEO and Chairman of Diebold, Inc. (1999-2005)" (list page) was committed "to helping Ohio deliver its electoral votes to the President." "the largest manufacturer of electronic voting equipment." "In December 2005, O'Dell left the company amid a" ... "investigation into insider trading at the company."
saint-louis.line: Mark this! Walden O'Dell, two engineering degrees from Saint Louis, ran Diebold, a maker of electronic voting equipment, and in two thousand three wrote that he was committed to helping Ohio deliver its electoral votes to the President. Subtlety, thy name is not O'Dell.

saint-louis.name: Steve Stenger
saint-louis.fact: Stenger, a Saint Louis University law graduate, resigned as St. Louis County Executive on April 29, 2019 after a federal indictment and was sentenced in August 2019 to 46 months in prison.
saint-louis.evidence: "Alma mater: Saint Louis University (J.D.) University of Missouri–St. Louis (B.Acy.)" "went to law school at St. Louis University." "Stenger announced his resignation on April 29, 2019, after being federally indicted on three counts" "honest services bribery and mail fraud." "In August 2019, Stenger was sentenced to 46 months in prison and to pay a fine of $250,000."
saint-louis.line: And Steve Stenger, of our law school, resigned as Saint Louis County Executive in twenty nineteen after a federal bribery indictment, and was sentenced to forty-six months in prison. Exit, pursued by a prosecutor.

saint-peters.name: Will Durant
saint-peters.fact: Durant graduated from Saint Peter's in 1907; he and his wife Ariel wrote the eleven-volume Story of Civilization and were jointly awarded the Pulitzer Prize in 1968 and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1977.
saint-peters.evidence: "Durant enrolled at Saint Peter's College (now Saint Peter's University), also in Jersey City, where he graduated in 1907." ... "best known for his eleven-volume work, The Story of Civilization," ... "It was written in collaboration with his wife, Ariel Durant, and published between 1935 and 1975." ... "he and his wife were jointly awarded the Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction in 1968 and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 1977."
saint-peters.line: Will Durant, class of nineteen oh seven, wrote the eleven-volume Story of Civilization with his wife Ariel. They shared a Pulitzer in sixty-eight and the Presidential Medal of Freedom in seventy-seven. Eleven volumes, my dears, and he gave her the credit.

saint-peters.name: Mary Ann McGuigan
saint-peters.years: Saint Peter's alumna (class year not given on the page)
saint-peters.fact: McGuigan was a 1997 National Book Award finalist.
saint-peters.evidence: [Saint_Peter's_University Notable alumni entry] "Mary Ann McGuigan, 1997 National Book Award finalist"
saint-peters.line: Mary Ann McGuigan, one of our own, was a National Book Award finalist in nineteen ninety-seven. A Peacock with a pen. I could not be prouder.

saint-peters.name: Joseph Patrick Tumulty
saint-peters.years: Saint Peter's alumnus (class year not given on the page)
saint-peters.fact: Tumulty served as chief of staff to President Woodrow Wilson.
saint-peters.evidence: [Saint_Peter's_University Notable alumni entry] "Joseph Patrick Tumulty, Chief of Staff to President Woodrow Wilson"
saint-peters.line: Joseph Tumulty went from Saint Peter's to the White House as chief of staff to President Woodrow Wilson. A Jersey City boy minding the president's door. Of course he was.

saint-peters.name: Albio Sires
saint-peters.years: Saint Peter's alumnus (class year not given on the page)
saint-peters.fact: Sires served as a United States Representative.
saint-peters.evidence: [Saint_Peter's_University Notable alumni entry] "United States Representatives Daniel J. Griffin, James A. Hamill, Edward J. Hart, Charles F. X. O'Brien, Albio Sires"
saint-peters.line: Albio Sires is one of five Peacocks on our list who went on to the United States House of Representatives. Five, my dears. We send them down to Washington by the carload.

saint-peters.name: Robert Menendez
saint-peters.years: Saint Peter's graduate, B.A. in political science (year not given on the page)
saint-peters.fact: Menendez, a Saint Peter's graduate, was convicted on July 16, 2024, of charges including bribery, resigned from the Senate in August 2024 and was sentenced on January 29, 2025, to 11 years in prison.
saint-peters.evidence: "Menendez became the first in his family to go to college, attending Saint Peter's College in Jersey City," ... "He graduated with a B.A. in political science and earned his Juris Doctor degree from Rutgers Law School in 1979." ... "On July 16, the jury convicted Menendez of all charges, including bribery, extortion, honest services fraud, obstruction of justice, and conspiracy." ... "Menendez resigned from the Senate in August 2024." ... "On January 29, 2025, Menendez was sentenced to 11 years in prison."
saint-peters.line: Then there is Senator Bob Menendez, political science. A jury convicted him of bribery in July of twenty twenty-four, he resigned the Senate that August, and a judge gave him eleven years. We claim him, my dears. We do not brag.

san-jose-state.name: Tommie Smith
san-jose-state.fact: Tommie Smith, B.A. 1969, is the gold medalist best known for the raised fist salute on the medal podium at the 1968 Summer Olympic Games.
san-jose-state.evidence: List entry, B.A. 1969: "gold medalist; best known for giving raised fist salute from the medalists' podium during the 1968 Summer Olympic Games"
san-jose-state.line: Tommie Smith, class of 1969. Gold medalist, and best known for raising his fist on the podium at the 1968 Olympics. He won the race, then he made the statement. Both shipped from San Jose.

san-jose-state.name: Harry Edwards
san-jose-state.fact: Harry Edwards, B.A. 1964, is professor emeritus of sociology at UC Berkeley and author of The Revolt of the Black Athlete.
san-jose-state.evidence: List entry, B.A. 1964: "professor emeritus of Sociology, University of California, Berkeley; author of The Revolt of the Black Athlete"
san-jose-state.line: Harry Edwards, class of 1964, wrote The Revolt of the Black Athlete and became professor emeritus of sociology at Berkeley. Some alumni write code. He wrote the documentation for a movement.

san-jose-state.name: Amy Tan
san-jose-state.known_for: author of The Joy Luck Club
san-jose-state.fact: Novelist Amy Tan, author of The Joy Luck Club, earned a B.A. in 1972 and an M.A. in 1973 from San Jose State.
san-jose-state.evidence: List entry, B.A. 1972, M.A. 1973: "novelist; author of The Joy Luck Club"
san-jose-state.line: Amy Tan earned her bachelor's here in 1972 and her master's in 1973, then wrote The Joy Luck Club. Two Spartan degrees, one novel everybody's mother has read. Solid return.

san-jose-state.name: Stevie Nicks
san-jose-state.fact: Stevie Nicks, the musician best known for Fleetwood Mac, attended San Jose State from 1968 to 1970.
san-jose-state.evidence: List entry, attended 1968–70: "musician best known for Fleetwood Mac"
san-jose-state.line: Stevie Nicks attended San Jose State from 1968 to 1970, then left and became the musician best known for Fleetwood Mac. Technically a dropout. We are keeping her in the release notes anyway.

san-jose-state.name: Gordon Moore
san-jose-state.fact: Gordon Moore, founder of Intel and creator of Moore's law, attended San Jose State in 1946-47.
san-jose-state.evidence: List entry, attended 1946–47: "founder of the Intel Corporation and creator of "Moore's law""
san-jose-state.line: Gordon Moore attended San Jose State in 1946 and 47 before founding Intel and giving us Moore's law. So the whole chip industry started with a Spartan transfer. Version one point oh was ours.

siena.name: William J. Kennedy
siena.fact: Kennedy, class of 1949, won the 1984 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novel Ironweed.
siena.evidence: [Siena_College article, alumni list] "William J. Kennedy '49 is an American author and journalist who won the 1984 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novel Ironweed."
siena.line: William Kennedy, class of forty-nine, an author and a newspaperman, won the nineteen eighty-four Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novel Ironweed. A Saint with a Pulitzer. Now that's a grand evening.

siena.name: Mae D'Agostino
siena.years: Siena alumna (class year not given on the page)
siena.fact: D'Agostino is a United States District Court judge for the Northern District of New York.
siena.evidence: [Siena_College article, alumni list] "Mae D'Agostino is a United States District Court judge for the United States District Court for the Northern District of New York."
siena.line: Mae D'Agostino, one of our own, sits as a United States District Court judge for the Northern District of New York. All rise, Saints, and I mean that fondly.

siena.name: George Deukmejian
siena.fact: Deukmejian graduated from Siena in 1949 with a B.A. in sociology and served as the 35th governor of California from 1983 to 1991.
siena.evidence: "For college, he graduated in 1949 with a B.A. in sociology from Siena College." ... "Born in New York, Deukmejian moved to California in 1955." ... "who served as the 35th governor of California from 1983 to 1991."
siena.line: George Deukmejian, born in New York, took a sociology degree from Siena in forty-nine, moved to California in fifty-five, and wound up the thirty-fifth governor out there. Long way from Loudonville, that.

siena.name: Wendy Moniz
siena.years: Siena alumna (class year not given on the page)
siena.fact: Moniz is a television actress known for Guiding Light, Nash Bridges, The Guardian, House of Cards and Yellowstone.
siena.evidence: [Siena_College article, alumni list] "Wendy Moniz is an American television actress known for her roles in Guiding Light, Nash Bridges, The Guardian, House of Cards, and Yellowstone."
siena.line: Wendy Moniz, a Saint, is the television actress you know from Guiding Light, Nash Bridges, House of Cards and Yellowstone. From the soaps to the ranch, she's been working steady.

siena.name: Anthony Brindisi
siena.fact: Brindisi, class of 2000, served as U.S. Representative from New York's 22nd congressional district from 2019 to 2021.
siena.evidence: [Siena_College article, alumni list] "Anthony Brindisi, class of 2000, served as U.S. Representative from New York's 22nd congressional district from 2019 to 2021."
siena.line: Anthony Brindisi, class of two thousand, represented New York's twenty-second district in Congress from twenty nineteen to twenty twenty-one. One term, Saints, but he got the pin.

southern-illinois.name: Dick Gregory
southern-illinois.years: attended on a track scholarship; no degree
southern-illinois.fact: Earned a track scholarship to SIU, left without a degree, ran for president in 1968, and wrote an autobiography that sold more than a million copies.
southern-illinois.evidence: Gregory earned a track scholarship to Southern Illinois University (SIU)... | he returned to the university but did not receive a degree. | Gregory was at the forefront of political activism in the 1960s, when he protested against the Vietnam War... | He was arrested multiple times and went on many hunger strikes. | Gregory ran for president in 1968 United States presidential election. | He later became a speaker and author, with his autobiography selling more than a million copies. | Richard Claxton Gregory (October 12, 1932 – August 19, 2017)
southern-illinois.line: Dick Gregory came to Carbondale on a track scholarship and left without a degree. He was at the forefront of activism in the sixties, arrested many times, a hunger striker, and in 1968 a candidate for president. The throne salutes him.

southern-illinois.name: L. Eudora Pettigrew
southern-illinois.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
southern-illinois.fact: Former president of SUNY Old Westbury and the first African-American president in the SUNY system.
southern-illinois.evidence: L. Eudora Pettigrew, former president of SUNY Old Westbury, first African-American president in the SUNY system
southern-illinois.line: L. Eudora Pettigrew, a Saluki, became president of SUNY Old Westbury, the first African-American president in the entire SUNY system. A dynasty begins with one.

southern-illinois.name: Roland Burris
southern-illinois.fact: Graduated in 1959, was the first African American elected to statewide office in Illinois, and was appointed to the U.S. Senate by Governor Rod Blagojevich in January 2009.
southern-illinois.evidence: He attended Southern Illinois University Carbondale, receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree in political science in 1959. | He was the first African American elected to statewide office in Illinois. | In January 2009, Governor Rod Blagojevich appointed Burris to the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Barack Obama... | Burris has built a mausoleum for himself in Oak Woods Cemetery on Chicago's South Side. | His tombstone reads 'TRAIL BLAZER' and includes a list of his accomplishments, with space left for future ones.
southern-illinois.line: Roland Burris, class of 1959, was the first African American elected statewide in Illinois. He has already built his own mausoleum, with a list of accomplishments carved in and space left for more. As a pharaoh, I respect the planning.

southern-illinois.name: Darryl Jones
southern-illinois.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
southern-illinois.evidence: Darryl Jones, bassist of The Rolling Stones
southern-illinois.line: Darryl Jones, a Saluki, is the bassist of The Rolling Stones. Even the oldest monuments need a steady foundation.

southern-illinois.name: Robert K. Weiss
southern-illinois.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
southern-illinois.evidence: Robert K. Weiss, producer of The Blues Brothers
southern-illinois.line: Robert K. Weiss of Southern Illinois produced The Blues Brothers. A mission from on high, delivered by a Saluki.

st-bonaventure.name: Dan Barry
st-bonaventure.fact: Barry graduated from St. Bonaventure in 1980, was part of the 1994 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting, and joined The New York Times in 1995.
st-bonaventure.evidence: "He graduated from St. Bonaventure University in 1980 with a bachelor's degree in mass communications" "1994 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting for exposing corruption in the Rhode Island court system" "joined The New York Times in 1995." "He is the author of five books." "Born: 1958 (age 67–68) New York City, U.S."
st-bonaventure.line: Dan Barry, class of nineteen eighty! His reporting on corruption in the Rhode Island courts took a nineteen ninety-four Pulitzer, he joined the New York Times in ninety-five, and he has written five books. What a splendid machine, the human pen!

st-bonaventure.name: Charles J. Hanley
st-bonaventure.fact: Hanley, class of 1968, is one of six St. Bonaventure alumni to have received the Pulitzer Prize.
st-bonaventure.evidence: "Six alumni of the university have received the Pulitzer Prize, including Dan Barry (1980)," "Bill Briggs (1985), Robert A. Dubill (1958), John Hanchette (1964), Charles J. Hanley (1968), and Brian Toolan (1972)."
st-bonaventure.line: Charles Hanley, class of nineteen sixty-eight, is one of six Bonaventure alumni to receive the Pulitzer Prize. Six! From one small campus! Somebody check the gauges!

st-bonaventure.name: John Hanchette
st-bonaventure.fact: Hanchette, class of 1964, is one of six St. Bonaventure alumni to have received the Pulitzer Prize.
st-bonaventure.evidence: "Six alumni of the university have received the Pulitzer Prize, including Dan Barry (1980)," "Bill Briggs (1985), Robert A. Dubill (1958), John Hanchette (1964), Charles J. Hanley (1968), and Brian Toolan (1972)."
st-bonaventure.line: And John Hanchette, class of nineteen sixty-four, another of our six Pulitzer Prize alumni. The Bonaventure prize engine, friends, simply keeps on whirring!

st-bonaventure.name: Carl Paladino
st-bonaventure.fact: Paladino, a St. Bonaventure B.A., was removed from his Buffalo school board seat by the New York State Education Department on August 17, 2017 for publicly disclosing confidential information.
st-bonaventure.evidence: "Paladino graduated from St. Bonaventure University for his B.A. and from the Syracuse University College of Law." "On August 17, 2017, following a public hearing, the New York State Education Department" "removed Paladino from his board seat for publicly disclosing confidential information obtained in executive session." "Paladino was defeated by Cuomo in the general election, 63%–33%." "Paladino is the chairman of Ellicott Development Co., a real estate development company he founded in 1973." "(born August 24, 1946)"
st-bonaventure.line: Carl Paladino, a Bonaventure graduate, founded a real estate company in nineteen seventy-three, lost a governor's race sixty-three to thirty-three, and in twenty seventeen was removed from his school board seat for disclosing confidential information. Some contraptions simply backfire!

stetson.name: Louis DeJoy
stetson.fact: DeJoy, who holds a Stetson BBA, was appointed postmaster general in 2020, issued a 2021 plan that lowered the speed of long-distance first class mail, and resigned on March 24, 2025.
stetson.evidence: "Stetson University (BBA)" ... "announced DeJoy's appointment as postmaster general and CEO" ... "such measures also resulted in the slow down of the mail service." ... "Lowering speed but increasing reliability for long-distance first class mail." ... "On March 24, 2025, DeJoy resigned his position."
stetson.line: Gather round for Louis DeJoy, Stetson business degree, Postmaster General starting in twenty twenty. His big plan lowered the speed of long-distance first class mail, and he resigned in twenty twenty-five. We claim him, friends. The thank-you card is still in transit.

stetson.name: Suzanne Kosmas
stetson.years: listed among Stetson notable people; year not shown
stetson.fact: Kosmas graduated from Stetson in 1998 and served in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2011.
stetson.line: Suzanne Kosmas graduated from Stetson, and Suzanne Kosmas went to Congress, two thousand nine to two thousand eleven. A Hatter under the Capitol dome. Hats off, and I mean that literally.

stetson.name: Bert Fish
stetson.years: listed among Stetson notable people; year not shown
stetson.fact: Fish studied at Stetson's law school and served as U.S. Ambassador to Egypt from 1933 to 1941.
stetson.line: Now here is a name. Bert Fish. A Stetson law man who served as United States Ambassador to Egypt from nineteen thirty-three to nineteen forty-one. From DeLand to the Nile. What a trip.

toledo.name: Fredric Baur
toledo.fact: Baur, a University of Toledo graduate, filed for a patent on the tubular Pringles container in 1966, and some of his ashes were buried in a Pringles can at his request.
toledo.evidence: Baur was a graduate of the University of Toledo in Toledo, Ohio, and received both his master's and PhD degrees at Ohio State University. | Baur filed for a patent for the tubular Pringles container ... in 1966, and it was granted in 1971. | Some of Baur's ashes were buried in a Pringles can at his request. | Fredric John Baur Jr. (July 14, 1918 – May 4, 2008)
toledo.line: Okay so Fredric Baur, Toledo grad, invented the Pringles can. Filed the patent in 1966. And when he died, some of his ashes were buried in a Pringles can, at his request. That is commitment to the bit!

toledo.name: Mildred D. Taylor
toledo.fact: Author Mildred D. Taylor is listed in the University of Toledo's class of 1965.
toledo.line: Mildred D. Taylor, class of 1965, is an author, and she's a Rocket. Class of 1965 and still on the shelf. Go read something by a Rocket.

toledo.name: Michael Sallah
toledo.years: alumnus per the list page; year not given
toledo.fact: Michael Sallah, a Washington Post investigative reporter, won the 2004 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting.
toledo.evidence: Michael Sallah | Washington Post investigative reporter; winner of 2004 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting
toledo.line: Michael Sallah won the 2004 Pulitzer Prize for Investigative Reporting, and he kept his. Toledo journalism, redeemed!

toledo.name: Danny Thomas
toledo.years: listed on the university's people page; year not given
toledo.fact: Danny Thomas was a nightclub comedian, actor and producer, and the founder of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.
toledo.evidence: Danny Thomas | Nightclub comedian; television and film actor and producer; founder of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital
toledo.line: Danny Thomas was a nightclub comedian, an actor, a producer, and the founder of St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. Funny and a founder of a children's hospital. Rockets do the most.

uc-davis.name: Patricia S. Cowings
uc-davis.fact: Patricia Cowings graduated from UC Davis in 1973 and in 1979 became the first African American woman scientist to be trained as an astronaut by NASA.
uc-davis.evidence: "In 1973, she graduated from the University of California, Davis, with a psychology degree." ... "She was the first American woman to be trained as a scientist astronaut by NASA" ... "she became the first African American woman scientist to be trained as an astronaut by NASA in 1979." ... "She is credited in creating and patenting the autogenic-feedback training exercise (AFTE) used to treat astronauts."
uc-davis.line: Patricia Cowings graduated from Davis in 1973. She was the first American woman trained as a scientist astronaut by NASA, and she patented a training exercise used to treat astronauts. Not bad for a cow town, folks.

uc-davis.name: Charles M. Rice
uc-davis.fact: UC Davis alumnus Charles M. Rice is a 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine laureate.
uc-davis.evidence: List entry: Charles M. Rice, "2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine laureate"
uc-davis.line: Charles Rice, an Aggie, won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2020. We don't brag much out here. But a Nobel is a Nobel, so I'll say it slow.

uc-davis.name: John S. Watson
uc-davis.fact: John S. Watson earned a B.A. in agricultural economics from UC Davis in 1978 and was chairman and CEO of Chevron from January 1, 2010 to January 31, 2018.
uc-davis.evidence: "In 1978, he graduated with a B.A. in Agricultural Economics from the University of California, Davis" ... "from January 1, 2010 to January 31, 2018" List entry: "former CEO of Chevron (2010–2018)"
uc-davis.line: John Watson, class of 1978, agricultural economics. Then he ran Chevron as chairman and CEO for eight years. We grow all kinds of things in Davis. An oil company boss was not on the seed packet.

uc-davis.name: Ethan Russell
uc-davis.fact: UC Davis alumnus Ethan Russell is the only rock photographer to have shot album covers for The Beatles, The Rolling Stones and The Who.
uc-davis.evidence: List entry: Ethan Russell, "the only rock photographer to have shot album covers for The Beatles, The Rolling Stones and The Who"
uc-davis.line: Ethan Russell, an Aggie, is the only rock photographer to shoot album covers for the Beatles, the Rolling Stones and the Who. All three. From Davis. I can't explain it either.

uc-davis.name: Mark Publicover
uc-davis.fact: UC Davis alumnus Mark Publicover, founder of JumpSport, invented the first affordable trampoline safety net enclosure.
uc-davis.evidence: List entry: Mark Publicover, "CEO and founder of JumpSport, inventor of the first affordable trampoline safety net enclosure"
uc-davis.line: Mark Publicover, an Aggie, invented the first affordable trampoline safety net enclosure. So if your kid bounced and stayed in the yard, thank Davis. We keep things fenced in out here.

uc-irvine.name: Yusef Komunyakaa
uc-irvine.fact: Yusef Komunyakaa, M.F.A. 1980, is a Pulitzer Prize-winning poet, honored for Neon Vernacular.
uc-irvine.evidence: Yusef Komunyakaa(M.F.A. 1980) – Pulitzer Prize-winning poet for Neon Vernacular
uc-irvine.line: Yusef Komunyakaa earned his master of fine arts at UC Irvine in nineteen eighty and won the Pulitzer Prize for poetry with Neon Vernacular. Anteaters write, and they win.

uc-irvine.name: Nazanin Boniadi
uc-irvine.fact: Nazanin Boniadi, B.S. in biological sciences 2003, is an actress and an official spokeswoman for Amnesty International.
uc-irvine.evidence: Nazanin Boniadi(B.S. 2003, biological sciences) – actress, official spokeswoman for Amnesty International
uc-irvine.line: Nazanin Boniadi took a biology degree here in two thousand three, became an actress, and serves as an official spokeswoman for Amnesty International. Lab coat, spotlight, human rights. Overachiever, and we mean it kindly.

uc-irvine.name: Arnnon Geshuri
uc-irvine.years: bachelor's in psychology; year not listed on source
uc-irvine.fact: Arnnon Geshuri, who holds a UC Irvine bachelor's in psychology, was involved in activities that became the subject of the High-Tech Employee Antitrust Litigation, which ended in a $415 million settlement paid by Adobe, Apple, Google and Intel.
uc-irvine.evidence: He received a bachelor's degree in psychology from the University of California, Irvine | Geshuri was involved in activities that later became the subject of the High-Tech Employee Antitrust Litigation case | a recruiter for Google who had tried to hire an Apple employee would be "terminated within the hour" for the action | a settlement of $415 million paid by Adobe, Apple, Google and Intel | In January 2016, he briefly served on the Wikimedia Foundation's board of trustees before stepping down under pressure.
uc-irvine.line: Psychology grad Arnnon Geshuri was involved in the activities behind the big tech employee antitrust case. Adobe, Apple, Google and Intel settled for four hundred fifteen million dollars. Technically ours. We checked twice.

uc-irvine.name: Chris Burden
uc-irvine.fact: Chris Burden (1946-2015) received his MFA at UC Irvine, where his 1971 master's thesis was locking himself in a school locker for five days; in 2008 he created Urban Light from 202 antique street lights.
uc-irvine.evidence: received his MFA at the University of California, Irvine—where his teachers included Robert Irwin—from 1969 to 1971. | Five Day Locker Piece (1971), was created for his master's thesis at the University of California, Irvine, where he locked himself in a school locker for five days. | In 2008, Burden created Urban Light, a sculptural work consisting of 202 found antique street lights | Christopher Lee Burden (April 11, 1946 – May 10, 2015) was an American artist working in
uc-irvine.line: For his master's thesis at UC Irvine in nineteen seventy one, Chris Burden locked himself in a school locker for five days. He later built Urban Light, two hundred two antique street lamps. And yes, he got the degree.

uc-irvine.name: Paul Mockapetris
uc-irvine.known_for: co-inventor of the Domain Name System
uc-irvine.fact: Paul Mockapetris, PhD in computer science 1982, is an Internet pioneer and co-inventor of the Domain Name System.
uc-irvine.evidence: Paul Mockapetris(PhD 1982, Computer Science) – Internet pioneer, co-inventor of the Domain Name System
uc-irvine.line: Every time you type a web address, thank an Anteater. Paul Mockapetris, computer science doctorate, nineteen eighty two, co-invented the Domain Name System.

uc-riverside.name: Marigold Linton
uc-riverside.fact: Marigold Linton, born in Banning in 1936, earned her B.A. in psychology at UC Riverside and in 1964 became the first Native American to earn a doctorate in psychology.
uc-riverside.evidence: Attending the newly opened University of California, Riverside, she earned straight As to obtain her B.A. in Psychology | to become in 1954 the first Indian from a California reservation to attend college | In 1964, she became the first Native American to earn a doctorate in psychology. | Marigold Lorelei Linton was born in Banning, California, in 1936 and is Cahuilla and Cupeño. | In 1974, she co–founded the National Indian Education Association.
uc-riverside.line: Marigold Linton came from Banning to a brand new UC Riverside and earned straight A's in psychology. In nineteen sixty four she became the first Native American to earn a doctorate in the field. Gather round for that one.

uc-riverside.name: Billy Collins
uc-riverside.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
uc-riverside.fact: Billy Collins, on UC Riverside's alumni list, was the eleventh United States Poet Laureate.
uc-riverside.evidence: Billy Collins– eleventh United States Poet Laureate
uc-riverside.line: Billy Collins, the eleventh Poet Laureate of the United States, is a Highlander. The country needed a poet and it called one of ours.

uc-riverside.name: Steve Breen
uc-riverside.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
uc-riverside.fact: Steve Breen, on UC Riverside's alumni list, is a 1998 Pulitzer Prize-winning editorial cartoonist.
uc-riverside.evidence: Steve Breen– 1998 Pulitzer Prize-winning editorial cartoonist
uc-riverside.line: Steve Breen drew his way to a Pulitzer Prize for editorial cartooning in nineteen ninety eight. A Highlander with a pen and an opinion. Dangerous combination.

uc-riverside.name: Ryan Holiday
uc-riverside.fact: Ryan Holiday, born 1987, dropped out of UC Riverside in his sophomore year at 19, was a director of marketing for American Apparel, and in 2012 published Trust Me, I'm Lying: Confessions of a Media Manipulator.
uc-riverside.evidence: He dropped out of the University of California, Riverside, in his sophomore year at 19 | Ryan Holiday was a director of marketing for American Apparel. | Holiday published his first book, Trust Me, I'm Lying: Confessions of a Media Manipulator, in 2012. | earned a name for himself pranking several media outlets by posing as a fake expert for stories
uc-riverside.line: Ryan Holiday dropped out of Riverside at nineteen, did marketing for American Apparel, and then wrote a book subtitled Confessions of a Media Manipulator. He posed as a fake expert to prank news outlets. He never made it to junior year here.

uc-riverside.name: Stefanie Schaeffer
uc-riverside.years: alumna; year not listed on source
uc-riverside.fact: Stefanie Schaeffer, on UC Riverside's alumni list, is a defense attorney and the 2006 winner of The Apprentice.
uc-riverside.evidence: Stefanie Schaeffer– defense attorney, 2006 winner of The Apprentice
uc-riverside.line: Stefanie Schaeffer, defense attorney and Highlander, won The Apprentice in two thousand six. She got hired on television. Make of that what you will.

uc-san-diego.name: Kate Rubins
uc-san-diego.fact: Kate Rubins, B.S. in molecular biology 1999, is a NASA astronaut and the first person to sequence DNA in space.
uc-san-diego.evidence: Kathleen (Kate) Rubins, B.S. (Molecular Biology), 1999, NASA astronaut, first person to sequence DNA in space
uc-san-diego.line: Kate Rubins, molecular biology, class of ninety nine, was the first person to sequence DNA in space. In space! That is the most UC San Diego sentence ever spoken.

uc-san-diego.name: Angela Davis
uc-san-diego.fact: Angela Davis, born 1944, earned a master's degree from UC San Diego in 1968; later prosecuted for three capital felonies, she was acquitted of all charges in 1972.
uc-san-diego.evidence: Davis earned a master's degree from the University of California, San Diego, in 1968. | Prosecuted for three capital felonies, including conspiracy to murder, | before being acquitted of all charges in 1972. | Angela Davis was born on January 26, 1944,
uc-san-diego.line: Angela Davis earned her master's degree at UC San Diego in nineteen sixty eight. Four years later, prosecuted for three capital felonies, she was acquitted of all charges. A Triton who never backed down.

uc-san-diego.name: Margaret Allen
uc-san-diego.fact: Margaret Allen, M.D. 1974, was the first female heart transplant surgeon.
uc-san-diego.evidence: Margaret Allen, MD (Medicine), 1974, first female heart transplant surgeon
uc-san-diego.line: Margaret Allen got her medical degree here in seventy four and became the first female heart transplant surgeon. First. Tritons literally put hearts in people.

uc-san-diego.name: Nick Woodman
uc-san-diego.fact: Nick Woodman, B.A. in visual arts 1997, was the highest paid U.S. chief executive in 2014, paying himself $235 million; in November 2016 GoPro cut an additional 15% of its workforce.
uc-san-diego.evidence: Nick Woodman, BA (Visual Arts), 1997, founder and CEO of GoPro | He earned a bachelor's degree in visual arts and a minor in creative writing from the University of California, San Diego | In 2014, Woodman was the highest paid US chief executive, paying himself $235 million | In November 2016, GoPro cut an additional 15% of its workforce
uc-san-diego.line: Nick Woodman, visual arts, ninety seven, founded GoPro and in twenty fourteen was the highest paid chief executive in America, paying himself two hundred thirty five million dollars. Two years later GoPro cut another fifteen percent of its workers. Great camera angle, Nick.

uc-san-diego.name: Mike Judge
uc-san-diego.fact: Mike Judge, B.S. in physics 1985, is an animator and director best known for Beavis and Butt-Head.
uc-san-diego.evidence: Mike Judge, BS (Physics), 1985, animator and director best known for Beavis and Butt-Head
uc-san-diego.line: Mike Judge has a physics degree from UC San Diego, class of eighty five. He used it to create Beavis and Butt-Head. Science is a big tent.

uc-santa-barbara.name: José M. Hernández
uc-santa-barbara.fact: José M. Hernández, born 1962, earned a Master of Science in electrical and computer engineering at UC Santa Barbara, was turned down eleven times by NASA before being selected in May 2004, and flew on Space Shuttle mission STS-128 in August 2009.
uc-santa-barbara.evidence: José M. Hernández, M.S. 1986 – participated with STS-128 | earned a Master of Science degree in electrical and computer engineering from the University of California, Santa Barbara | As a child, Hernández worked alongside his family and other farmworkers throughout the fields of California | He attended many schools and didn't learn to speak English until he was 12. | After three years and being turned down eleven times for astronaut training by NASA, Hernández was selected in May 2004. | Hernández was on the Space Shuttle mission STS-128 in August 2009.
uc-santa-barbara.line: José Hernández worked the fields of California as a kid and didn't speak English until he was twelve. He got his master's at UCSB, NASA turned him down eleven times, and in two thousand nine he rode the shuttle anyway.

uc-santa-barbara.name: Chanel Miller
uc-santa-barbara.fact: Chanel Miller, B.A. 2014, is the author of Know My Name: A Memoir.
uc-santa-barbara.evidence: Chanel Miller, B.A. 2014 – author of Know My Name: A Memoir and Emily Doe of People v. Turner
uc-santa-barbara.line: Chanel Miller, class of twenty fourteen, wrote the memoir Know My Name. It took real courage to put her name on that book, and Gauchos are proud she's one of us.

uc-santa-barbara.name: Dionicio Morales
uc-santa-barbara.fact: Dionicio Morales, who attended UC Santa Barbara, was a Latino civil rights leader.
uc-santa-barbara.evidence: Dionicio Morales, attended – Latino civil rights leader
uc-santa-barbara.line: Dionicio Morales attended UC Santa Barbara and became a Latino civil rights leader. Not everything that starts on this campus ends up at the beach.

uc-santa-barbara.name: Jack Johnson
uc-santa-barbara.fact: Jack Johnson, B.A. 1997, is a four-time platinum singer-songwriter and musician.
uc-santa-barbara.evidence: Jack Johnson, B.A. 1997 – four-time platinum singer-songwriter and musician, In Between Dreams and On and On
uc-santa-barbara.line: Jack Johnson, class of ninety seven, is a four-time platinum singer-songwriter. If you've ever heard an acoustic guitar near a bonfire, you've basically attended UCSB.

uic.name: Carol Moseley Braun
uic.fact: Class of 1969; the first African-American woman elected to the U.S. Senate.
uic.evidence: Carol Moseley Braun, 1969, politician and lawyer and the first African-American woman elected to the US Senate
uic.line: Carol Moseley Braun. Class of 1969. Lawyer, politician, and the first African-American woman ever elected to the United States Senate. Chicago, she started right here.

uic.name: Sheila Tlou
uic.fact: Class of 1990; Botswana specialist in HIV/AIDS and women's health, nursing educator and former Minister of Health.
uic.evidence: Sheila Tlou 1990, Botswana specialist in HIV/AIDS and women's health, nursing educator and former Minister of Health
uic.line: Sheila Tlou left U I C in 1990 and became Botswana's Minister of Health, a nursing educator, and a specialist in H I V and women's health. That, my friends, is a flame that travels.

uic.name: Tony Podesta
uic.fact: Co-founded Podesta Associates in 1988, announced on October 30, 2017 that he would leave the Podesta Group, and was reportedly hired by Huawei as a lobbyist in July 2021.
uic.evidence: Tony Podesta, class of '67, prominent Washington lobbyist, founder of the Podesta Group | In 1988 Tony and John Podesta founded Podesta Associates... | Clients of the firm have included Google, Wells Fargo, General Electric, Boeing... | On October 30, 2017, Podesta announced that he would leave the Podesta Group. | On July 23, 2021, Huawei reportedly hired Podesta as consultant and lobbyist...
uic.line: Tony Podesta, class of 67. Prominent Washington lobbyist. Clients included Google, Wells Fargo, General Electric and Boeing. He left his own firm in October 2017, and by 2021 Huawei had reportedly hired him. We taught him political science. The rest was extra credit.

uic.name: Bernard Shaw
uic.fact: Class of 1968; anchor for CNN from 1980 until his retirement in 2001.
uic.evidence: Bernard Shaw, 1968, anchor for CNN from 1980 to his retirement in 2001
uic.line: Bernard Shaw, class of 1968, anchored C N N from 1980 until he retired in 2001. Twenty-one years in the chair. I am only getting warmed up.

uic.name: Mike Nawrocki
uic.fact: Earned a B.S. in 1992 and co-created, wrote and directed the animated series VeggieTales.
uic.evidence: Mike Nawrocki, (BS 1992), co-creator, writer and director of the animated series VeggieTales; voice of Larry the Cucumb...
uic.line: Mike Nawrocki took his degree here in 1992, then co-created, wrote and directed VeggieTales. Yes, the talking vegetables. Chicago contains multitudes.

umass.name: George Ruffin Bridgeforth
umass.fact: George Ruffin Bridgeforth, class of 1901, was a Tuskegee Institute agriculturist and the first Black graduate of UMass Amherst.
umass.evidence: George Ruffin Bridgeforth: 1901, Tuskegee Institute agriculturist and first Black graduate of UMass Amherst
umass.line: George Ruffin Bridgeforth, class of 1901, was the first Black graduate of UMass Amherst, and went on to be an agriculturist at Tuskegee Institute. First one through the door, over a century ago. Respect.

umass.name: Madeleine Kunin
umass.fact: Madeleine Kunin, class of 1956, was the first female governor of Vermont and a former U.S. ambassador to Switzerland.
umass.evidence: Madeleine Kunin: 1956, first female governor of Vermont and former U.S. ambassador to Switzerland (1985–1991)
umass.line: Madeleine Kunin, class of 1956, became the first woman governor of Vermont and a U S ambassador to Switzerland. Amherst to the statehouse to the Alps. Not a bad road trip.

umass.name: Catherine Coleman
umass.fact: Astronaut Catherine Coleman earned a Ph.D. from UMass Amherst in 1991.
umass.line: Catherine Coleman got her doctorate here in 1991 and became an astronaut. So yeah, the commute from Amherst can get pretty long.

umass.name: Jack Welch
umass.fact: Welch earned a chemical engineering degree at UMass Amherst in 1957; GE had 411,000 employees at the end of 1980 and 299,000 at the end of 1985, and he received a $417 million severance payment.
umass.evidence: Late in his senior year, Welch was accepted to University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he studied chemical engineering. | He graduated in 1957 with a Bachelor of Science degree in chemical engineering | he was dubbed "Neutron Jack" (in reference to the neutron bomb) for eliminating employees while leaving buildings intact. | GE had 411,000 employees at the end of 1980, and 299,000 at the end of 1985. | he received a severance payment of $417 million; at that time this was the largest such payment in business history. | John Francis Welch Jr. (November 19, 1935 – March 1, 2020) || List page: Jack Welch: 1957, retired CEO of General Electric
umass.line: Jack Welch, class of 1957. They called him Neutron Jack, because the employees vanished and the buildings stayed. G E went from 411,000 workers to 299,000 in five years, and he left with 417 million in severance. Our chemical engineer, everybody.

umass.name: Ryan Salame
umass.fact: Salame earned a B.A. in economics from UMass Amherst in 2015, pleaded guilty to campaign finance and illegal money-transmitting charges, and in May 2024 was sentenced to 7.5 years in federal prison.
umass.evidence: and also Bachelor of Arts in economics from the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 2015. | pleaded guilty to violating campaign finance laws and operating an illegal money-transmitting business. | Despite prosecutors recommending a term of 5-7 years, in May 2024 Salame was sentenced to 7.5 years in federal prison. | Salame invested over $6 million in Lenox, Massachusetts restaurants and real estate. || List page: Ryan Salame: 2015, former CEO of FTX Digital Markets, a FTX subsidiary based in the Bahamas
umass.line: Ryan Salame, economics, class of 2015, ran an F T X subsidiary in the Bahamas. He pleaded guilty to campaign finance and illegal money-transmitting charges and got seven and a half years in May 2024. Nine years from diploma to sentencing. Efficient.

unlv.name: Shelley Berkley
unlv.fact: Shelley Berkley, the first member of her family to attend college, graduated from UNLV with honors in 1972 and represented Nevada's 1st congressional district from 1999 to 2013.
unlv.evidence: "she became the first member of her family to attend college" ... "when she enrolled as an undergraduate at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas" ... "Elected student body president of the Consolidated Students of the University of Nevada, Las Vegas her senior year" ... "Shelley graduated with honors in 1972, earning a B.A. in political science." ... "Berkley represented Nevada's 1st congressional district from 1999 to 2013" ... "She was sworn-in as mayor on December 4."
unlv.line: Shelley Berkley was the first in her family to attend college. She became our student body president, graduated with honors in 1972, went to Congress, and then got sworn in as mayor. Vegas loves a headliner who works her way up.

unlv.name: Eric Whitacre
unlv.fact: Composer Eric Whitacre could not read music when he began training as a UNLV undergraduate; his Virtual Choir 4 gathered 8,409 videos from 5,905 people in 101 countries.
unlv.evidence: "Though he was unable to read music at the time, Whitacre began his full musical training while he was an undergraduate at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas." ... "He eventually earned a bachelor's degree in Music Composition." ... "Virtual Choir 4, "Fly to Paradise", contains 8,409 videos from 5,905 people from 101 countries." ... "This album won the Grammy for Best Choral Performance in 2012."
unlv.line: Eric Whitacre arrived at UNLV unable to read music. He left with a composition degree, and later built a virtual choir with singers from a hundred and one countries. Now that, darlings, is a residency.

unlv.name: Jimmy Kimmel
unlv.fact: Comedian and talk show host Jimmy Kimmel attended UNLV but did not graduate; he received an honorary degree in 2013.
unlv.evidence: List entry: "comedian and talk show host (did not graduate; received honorary degree in 2013)"
unlv.line: Jimmy Kimmel attended UNLV and did not graduate. In 2013 we gave him an honorary degree anyway. In this town, sometimes the house lets you win.

unlv.name: Anthony E. Zuiker
unlv.years: alumnus (b. 1968; year not given on source)
unlv.fact: UNLV alumnus Anthony E. Zuiker, born 1968, is the creator and executive producer of CSI.
unlv.evidence: List entry: Anthony E. Zuiker (b. 1968), "creator and executive producer of CSI"
unlv.line: Anthony Zuiker, a Rebel, is the creator and executive producer of CSI. So that whole crime lab empire started with one of ours. Vegas does love a good reveal.

unlv.name: Miki Sudo
unlv.years: alumna (b. 1985; year not given on source)
unlv.fact: UNLV alumna Miki Sudo, born 1985, is a competitive eater.
unlv.line: Miki Sudo, a Rebel, is a competitive eater. In a city built on the all you can eat buffet, somebody finally took that as a challenge.

utah-valley.name: Akwasi Frimpong
utah-valley.fact: Akwasi Frimpong graduated from Utah Valley with honors in marketing in 2013 and in 2018 became the first skeleton athlete from Ghana and the first black male skeleton athlete in Olympic history.
utah-valley.evidence: He graduated from Utah Valley University (UVU) with honors in marketing and a minor in business management in 2013. | In 2018, Frimpong became the first skeleton athlete from Ghana, | the first black male skeleton athlete in Olympic history.
utah-valley.line: Akwasi Frimpong graduated from Utah Valley with honors in twenty thirteen. Five years later he became the first skeleton athlete from Ghana, and the first black man to race skeleton in Olympic history. Headfirst, on ice. Bless him.

utah-valley.name: Thayne Jasperson
utah-valley.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
utah-valley.fact: Thayne Jasperson, on Utah Valley's alumni list, is a Broadway actor, singer and choreographer most notable for the musical Hamilton.
utah-valley.evidence: Thayne Jasperson– Broadway actor, singer, and choreographer, most notable for Hamilton (musical)
utah-valley.line: Thayne Jasperson went from Utah Valley to Broadway as an actor, singer and choreographer, and he's best known for Hamilton. Orem to the room where it happens.

utah-valley.name: Trevor Milton
utah-valley.years: attended; dropped out after one semester
utah-valley.fact: Trevor Milton, born 1982, enrolled at Utah Valley but dropped out after one semester, founded Nikola in 2015, was found guilty in October 2022 on one count of securities fraud and two counts of wire fraud, and received a full presidential pardon in March 2025.
utah-valley.evidence: He later enrolled at Utah Valley University but dropped out after one semester and then moved to the city of St. George. | In 2015, Milton founded Nikola Motor Company in Salt Lake City, initially known as Bluegentech, | In October 2022, he was found guilty on one count of securities fraud and two counts of wire fraud | In March 2025, he was given a full pardon by President Donald Trump. | On February 19, 2025, Nikola Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection
utah-valley.line: Trevor Milton was with us for one semester. He founded Nikola, he was found guilty of securities fraud and wire fraud in twenty twenty two, and he was pardoned in twenty twenty five. Nikola went bankrupt. One semester, I'll say again.

utah-valley.name: Brandon Fugal
utah-valley.years: alumnus; year not listed on source
utah-valley.fact: Brandon Fugal, on Utah Valley's alumni list, is a businessman and the owner of Skinwalker Ranch.
utah-valley.evidence: Brandon Fugal– businessman and owner of Skinwalker Ranch.
utah-valley.line: Brandon Fugal is a Utah Valley alum and a businessman, and he owns Skinwalker Ranch. I won't tell you what's out there, because I truly do not know.

utah-valley.name: Chelsie Hightower
utah-valley.years: alumna; year not listed on source
utah-valley.fact: Chelsie Hightower, on Utah Valley's alumni list, was a professional dancer on Dancing with the Stars and So You Think You Can Dance.
utah-valley.evidence: Chelsie Hightower– a professional dancer on TV series Dancing with the Stars and So You Think You Can Dance
utah-valley.line: Chelsie Hightower danced as a professional on Dancing with the Stars and on So You Think You Can Dance. She's a Wolverine, and yes, we think she can.

utep.name: Rubén Salazar
utep.fact: Rubén Salazar graduated from Texas Western College in 1954 with a journalism degree and was the first Mexican-American journalist from mainstream media to cover the Chicano community.
utep.evidence: "Salazar attended the Texas Western College, graduating in 1954 with a degree in journalism." ... "Salazar was the first Mexican-American journalist from mainstream media to cover the Chicano community." ... "killed by a Los Angeles County Sheriff's deputy during the National Chicano Moratorium March against the Vietnam War."
utep.line: Rubén Salazar got his journalism degree here in 1954, back when we were Texas Western. He was the first Mexican-American journalist in mainstream media to cover the Chicano community. Un orgullo, El Paso. One of ours told the story first.

utep.name: Ginger Kerrick
utep.fact: UTEP alumna Ginger Kerrick is a physicist and the first Hispanic female NASA Flight Director at Johnson Space Center.
utep.evidence: List entry: Ginger Kerrick, "physicist and first Hispanic female NASA Flight Director at NASA's Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center"
utep.line: Ginger Kerrick, a Miner and a physicist, became the first Hispanic female flight director at NASA's Johnson Space Center. When Houston answers, sometimes it's El Paso talking. Ándale!

utep.name: Martha E. Bernal
utep.fact: UTEP alumna Martha E. Bernal was the first Latina to earn a PhD in psychology in the United States.
utep.evidence: List entry: Martha E. Bernal, "psychologist; first Latina to earn a PhD in psychology in the U.S."
utep.line: Martha Bernal, one of ours, was the first Latina to earn a PhD in psychology in the United States. First one through the door, and she started right here on the border.

utep.name: Charles A. Steen
utep.years: class of 1943 (College of Mines and Metallurgy)
utep.fact: Charles Steen earned a geology degree from the College of Mines in 1943, struck uranium on July 6, 1952, built a $250,000 mansion, and filed for bankruptcy in 1968.
utep.evidence: "in 1940 transferred to the College of Mines and Metallurgy of the University of Texas" ... "receiving a Bachelor of Arts degree in geology in 1943." ... "On July 6, 1952, Steen reached uranium, however he didn't realize until three weeks later." ... "In Moab, Steen built a $250,000 hilltop mansion to replace his tarpaper shack" ... "flying to Salt Lake City in his private plane for weekly rumba lessons" ... "In 1968 he filed for bankruptcy after the Internal Revenue Service seized his assets to pay back taxes." List entry: "geologist whose Mi Vida Mine discovery started the American Uranium Boom of the 1950s"
utep.line: Charles Steen, geology, class of 1943. In 1952 he struck uranium, swapped a tarpaper shack for a mansion, and flew his own plane to weekly rumba lessons. By 1968 he'd filed for bankruptcy. A real Miner, y'all. Boom and bust.

utep.name: John D. Olivas
utep.fact: John D. Olivas was the first UTEP alumnus to be selected as an astronaut by NASA.
utep.evidence: List entry: John D. Olivas, "first UTEP alumnus to be selected as an astronaut by NASA"
utep.line: John Olivas was the first UTEP alumnus picked by NASA to be an astronaut. Miners usually dig down, right? This one went the other way. Órale!

valparaiso.name: Alys McKey Bryant
valparaiso.years: attended; years not given on source
valparaiso.fact: Attended Valparaiso and on July 31, 1913 became the first woman to fly in Canada; she also set a women's altitude record of 2,900 feet.
valparaiso.evidence: She attended Valparaiso University. | Heading even further north, she became the first woman to fly in Canada on July 31, 1913. | While in Seattle, Bryant also set an altitude record for women, reaching 2,900 feet. | Bryant was born in rural Indiana on April 28, 1880. | Bryant died on September 6, 1954.
valparaiso.line: Alys McKey Bryant attended Valparaiso, and on July thirty-first, 1913, she became the first woman to fly in Canada. She set a women's altitude record too, twenty-nine hundred feet. A true Valkyrie, with her own wings.

valparaiso.name: George William Norris
valparaiso.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
valparaiso.fact: United States senator from Nebraska known as the father of the Tennessee Valley Authority.
valparaiso.evidence: George William Norris, United States senator from Nebraska; "father" of the Tennessee Valley Authority
valparaiso.line: George William Norris studied at Valparaiso and became a United States senator from Nebraska. They call him the father of the Tennessee Valley Authority. Public power, Beacons, for the public.

valparaiso.name: Carl Glennis Roberts
valparaiso.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
valparaiso.fact: Carl Glennis Roberts (1886–1950) was a surgeon, gynecologist and civil rights activist.
valparaiso.evidence: Carl Glennis Roberts (1886–1950), surgeon, gynecologist, and civil rights activist
valparaiso.line: Carl Glennis Roberts, born 1886, was a surgeon, a gynecologist, and a civil rights activist. He healed people and he fought for them. Valparaiso is proud to carry his name on its rolls.

valparaiso.name: JoBe Cerny
valparaiso.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
valparaiso.fact: Character actor and the voice of the Pillsbury Doughboy.
valparaiso.evidence: JoBe Cerny, character actor and voice of the Pillsbury Doughboy
valparaiso.line: JoBe Cerny of Valparaiso is a character actor and the voice of the Pillsbury Doughboy. I have faced many warriors, and none giggle like that one.

valparaiso.name: Lowell Thomas
valparaiso.years: alumnus; class year not given on source
valparaiso.fact: Author and World War I war correspondent who made T. E. Lawrence internationally famous.
valparaiso.evidence: Lowell Thomas, author, war correspondent during World War I who made T. E. Lawrence internationally famous, and recipient...
valparaiso.line: Lowell Thomas was an author and a war correspondent in World War One, the man who made T. E. Lawrence internationally famous. Every hero needs a herald, and this one was a Valpo man.

vcu.name: Grace E. Harris
vcu.fact: Harris was denied admission to Richmond Professional Institute in 1954 on the basis of race, completed her Master of Social Work there in 1960, and joined the VCU faculty in 1967.
vcu.evidence: "Harris was originally denied admission to Richmond Professional Institute in 1954 on the basis of race." vcu.line: Grace Harris was denied admission in nineteen fifty-four because of her race. She came back, finished her master's in social work in nineteen sixty, joined the faculty in sixty-seven, and rose to acting president. That is how you flip the record.

western-michigan.name: Merze Tate
western-michigan.fact: In 1927 Merze Tate became the first African-American to earn a bachelor's degree from Western, and she was later the first African-American woman to attend the University of Oxford.
western-michigan.evidence: In 1927, she became the first African-American to earn a bachelor's degree from the institution. | She was the first African-American graduate of Western Michigan Teachers College | first African-American woman to attend the University of Oxford | first African-American woman to earn a Ph.D. in government and international relations from Harvard University | Vernie Merze Tate (February 6, 1905 – June 27, 1996)
western-michigan.line: Merze Tate, hon. In 1927 she was the first African-American to earn a bachelor's degree here. Then the first African-American woman to attend Oxford, then the first to earn a Harvard doctorate in government. That's three firsts. I counted.

western-michigan.line: Loretta Long earned her bachelor's here in 1960 and went on to play Susan Robinson on Sesame Street. If you learned your letters from Susan, you learned them from a Bronco.

wright-state.name: Michael R. Barratt
wright-state.fact: Michael Barratt completed a Master of Science in aerospace medicine in 1991 in a program jointly run by Wright State, NASA and Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, and spent 198 days in space on his first flight in 2009.
wright-state.evidence: In 1991, Barratt completed both a residency and a Master of Science in aerospace medicine jointly run by Wright State University, NASA, and Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. ... Barratt returned to Earth on October 11, 2009 after spending 198 days, 16 hours, and 42 minutes in space ... and also served as the pilot on the SpaceX Crew-8 mission, which launched on March 4, 2024. ... Michael Reed Barratt (born April 16, 1959) is an American physician and a NASA astronaut.
wright-state.line: Okay, my favorite. Michael Barratt finished a master's in aerospace medicine here in 1991, a program run with NASA and Wright-Patterson. Then he spent 198 days in space, and in 2024 he piloted a SpaceX crew mission. A doctor who flies the spaceship!

wright-state.name: Hannah Beachler

For her work on Black Panther, Beachler became the first African-American to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Production Design, as well as the first to win the category. ... She also worked on the 2015 Rocky film Creed, the Miles Davis biopic Miles Ahead (2015), and Moonlight (2016).
wright-state.line: Hannah Beachler studied film right here in Dayton. For Black Panther she became the first African-American ever nominated for the production design Oscar, and the first to win it. She designed that world. Dayton takes a little credit.

youngstown-state.evidence: a second Master's degree in counseling from Youngstown State University in 1976. ... expelled from the House on July 24, 2002, after being convicted of 10 felony counts including taking bribes, filing false tax returns, racketeering, and forcing his congressional staff to perform chores at his farm in Ohio and houseboat in Washington, D.C. ... He usually ended his speeches with the phrase "beam me up", a Star Trek reference. ... May 8, 1941 – September 27, 2014
youngstown-state.line: Jim Traficant. Master's in counseling, 1976. Convicted on ten felony counts in 2002, bribes and racketeering. The House threw him out, 420 to 1. He got eight years. He used to end speeches with beam me up. They did.
